title: Cyclotomic KLR Algebras and Highest-Weight Categorification

items.title: The cyclotomic KLR quotient at a dominant integral weight
items.statement:
Fix a symmetrizable Cartan datum with finite color set $I$ and no imaginary
simple roots, a KLR datum $Q=(Q_{ij})_{i\ne j}$ satisfying (Q1)-(Q4), and a
field $k$ placed in degree zero
([[def-quiver-hecke-klr-algebra-for-a-symmetrizable-cartan-datum]],
[[def-symmetrizable-cartan-datum-for-a-quantum-group]]); let
$R=\bigoplus_{\beta\in Q_+}R(\beta)$ be the resulting graded KLR algebra, with
its idempotents $e(\nu)$, dots $x_a$, crossings $\tau_a$ and degrees
$\deg x_a=2d_{\nu_a}$, $\deg\tau_a=-b_{\nu_a\nu_{a+1}}$
([[def-klr-grading-and-diagrammatic-composition]]). Let $\Lambda$ be a
dominant integral weight and put $\lambda_i:=\langle h_i,\Lambda\rangle\ge0$
([[def-kac-moody-integral-and-dominant-integral-weights]]).

**Cyclotomic data.** For every color $i$ choose a monic polynomial
$a_i(u)\in k[u]$ of degree exactly $\lambda_i$
([[def-polynomial-ring-over-a-commutative-ring]]); the standard choice made
below is $a_i(u)=u^{\lambda_i}$. For $n\ge1$ write
$$a(x_s)=\sum_{\nu\in I^n}a_{\nu_s}(x_s)e(\nu)\qquad(1\le s\le n),$$
the element of $R_n(Q)$ that acts on the $\nu$-component by the monic
polynomial $a_{\nu_s}$ in the dot at position $s$.

**The cyclotomic quotient.** For $\beta\in Q_+$ define $J_a(\beta)$ to be the
two-sided ideal of $R(\beta)$ generated by the first-strand elements
$a_{\nu_1}(x_1)e(\nu)$, $\nu\in I^\beta$; equivalently
$$J_a(\beta)=\sum_{\nu\in I^\beta}R(\beta)\,a_{\nu_1}(x_1)e(\nu)\,R(\beta),$$
and put
$$R_a^\Lambda(\beta):=R(\beta)/J_a(\beta),\qquad R_a^\Lambda(0):=k .$$
The **cyclotomic KLR algebra** is the direct sum
$R_a^\Lambda:=\bigoplus_{\beta\in Q_+}R_a^\Lambda(\beta)$; it carries the
local units $e(\beta)=\sum_{\nu\in I^\beta}e(\nu)$, which act as the identity
on $R_a^\Lambda(\beta)$ and annihilate the other summands, and it is a
$k$-algebra with these orthogonal idempotents.

**Standard choice and grading.** The STANDARD choice $a_i(u)=u^{\lambda_i}$ is
used throughout the graded categorification, duality-normalization and based
statements below; for it we write $R^\Lambda:=R^\Lambda_a$. Under the standard
choice each individual first-strand generator
$x_1^{\lambda_{\nu_1}}e(\nu)$ is homogeneous of degree
$2d_{\nu_1}\lambda_{\nu_1}$ in the grading of
[[def-klr-grading-and-diagrammatic-composition]], so the ideal $J_a(\beta)$
and the quotient $R^\Lambda(\beta)$ are graded, and $R^\Lambda$ is a
$\mathbb Z$-graded algebra with local units. The sum $a(x_1)$ itself need not
have one common degree across different colors, and no single degree is
assigned to it.

**Boundary of the definition.** Arbitrary monic polynomials with lower
coefficients in degree-zero $k$ give an UNGRADED deformation $R_a^\Lambda$;
nilpotent dots, homogeneous trace degree and the highest-weight graded $K_0$
identification are not asserted for that branch, and the ungraded branch is
used only where a statement explicitly says so. Finite dimension, finite root
strings, ordinary projectivity and symmetry of the standard quotient have the
separately stated monic conclusions below. The cyclotomic relation is imposed
on the FIRST strand, and cyclotomic induction appends strands on the RIGHT
([[def-cyclotomic-klr-induction-and-restriction-functors]]); this convention
fixes the side on which the quotient map acts throughout the page.

This definition uses no choice.
items.strategy: The idempotents isolate the individual generators, so the displayed ideal also equals $R(\beta)a(x_1)R(\beta)$ when the latter expression is restricted to this block. In the standard choice each isolated generator is homogeneous; this proves the grading, without falsely assigning one degree to their sum. Over a degree-zero field a monic homogeneous polynomial of positive dot degree is the pure power. Lower monic coefficients therefore require forgetting the grading. The example $\lambda_i=2$, $a_i=u(u-1)$ gives $k\oplus k$ at root $\alpha_i$, so its two projective classes cannot be the one-dimensional middle weight of $V(2)$; the standard graded hypothesis is substantive. The rank-zero convention avoids an undefined first letter of the empty word. This definition uses no choice.

items.title: The minimal-parabolic KLR diagram proof category
items.statement:
Fix a symmetrizable Cartan datum with real simple roots (so $a_{ii}=2$ for
every color $i$), a field $k$ placed in degree zero, and weighted-homogeneous
KLR polynomials $Q_{jk}$ satisfying (Q1)-(Q4) as in
[[def-quiver-hecke-klr-algebra-for-a-symmetrizable-cartan-datum]]; write
$b_{jk}=d_j a_{jk}=b_{kj}$. Fix a color $i$. The **minimal-parabolic KLR
diagram proof category** $\mathcal P_i$ is the additive graded $k$-linear
2-category of weighted oriented diagrams described by the generators, objects
and equations below.

**Generators and composition.** The objects are the weights
$\mu\in P$. The generating $1$-morphisms are the downward generators
$G_j:\mu\to\mu-\alpha_j$, one for every color $j$, and the single upward
generator $H_i:\mu\to\mu+\alpha_i$. Horizontal composition reads chronological
negative words from the vacuum outward. Take additive sums of objects and
grading shifts, and use idempotent completion when speaking of word
projectives. The generator $H_i$ denotes **normalized projective
restriction**: in the polynomial flag realization at input weight $h=\langle
h_i,\mu\rangle$ it is basic reversed flag restriction shifted by
$-d_i(1+h)$; it is distinct from unshifted basic restriction.

**The graded 2-morphism spaces.** The weights are 0-objects. A 1-morphism
is a finite composable word in the $G_j,H_i$, with its specified source and
target weights; identities are empty words. For parallel words $u,v$, define
$\operatorname{Hom}^n(u,v)$ as the degree-$n$ part of the $k$-span of formal
oriented string diagrams generated by the dots, downward crossings and four
units/counits below, modulo the displayed local relations. Every strand is
labeled by its color, and its direction is downward for $G_j$ and upward for
$H_i$. The top boundary is the source word and the bottom boundary the target
word. Regions carry the unique weights obtained from the outside source
weight by the indicated simple-root changes. Diagrams are generic: transverse
double crossings, isolated dots and nondegenerate cups/caps, with no triple
crossing or dot at a crossing/extremum. Oppositely oriented crossings denote
the specified adjunction mates of a downward crossing, not new generators.
Use planar isotopies preserving the ordered oriented local events; moving
a crossing past an extremum uses the mate relations below. Vertical
composition is stacking and horizontal composition is juxtaposition at a
common weight; degrees add under either operation. The interchange relation
and bilinearity are imposed. A degree-$n$ map from $u$ to $v$ is a degree-zero
map $u\{n\}\to v$ with the internal-shift convention of the grading supplier.
Additive sums, shifts and idempotent completion have their usual graded
2-category meanings applied to these Hom spaces.

**Degrees and the native crossing.** Dots have degree $2d_j$ and downward
crossings have degree $-b_{jk}$, matching the grading of
[[def-klr-grading-and-diagrammatic-composition]]. The native crossing is
$\tau$, with native equal-color divided difference
$(f-sf)/(x_1-x_2)$; for expressing the source diagram equations put
$\kappa=-\tau$ for **every** color pair, retaining dots, idempotents and $Q$.
Thus the native cubic braid numerator is globally opposite to the source
numerator, while the quadratic $Q$ is unchanged. Impose the full downward KLR
relations of the cited Definition.

**Adjunctions and the rank-one matrix.** At input $i$-weight $h$, the first
unit $1\to H_iG_i$ and the second counit $H_iG_i\to1$ have degree
$d_i(1-h)$; the first counit $G_iH_i\to1$ and the second unit
$1\to G_iH_i$ have degree $d_i(1+h)$. Impose both adjunction triangles with
their adjacent input-weight shifts and cyclicity of the dot. For $h\ge0$
prescribe the degree-zero rank-one matrix
$$H_iG_i\cong G_iH_i\oplus\bigoplus_{r=0}^{h-1}1\{d_i(1-h+2r)\};$$
for $h<0$ prescribe
$$G_iH_i\cong H_iG_i\oplus\bigoplus_{r=0}^{-h-1}1\{d_i(1+h+2r)\}.$$
The off-diagonal crossing component is the cup--source-crossing--cap
transfer, and the identity columns and rows are the indicated dotted
units/counits. Adjoin its actual inverse blocks, requiring both matrix inverse
equations; the dotted dual rows and columns are the finite triangular
coefficient convolution determined by bubble inversion, and the crossing
block satisfies the local cross-and-cap equations. In particular, at $h<0$,
if $r_h:G_iH_i\to H_iG_i\oplus D_{-h}$ is this matrix, then $r_h^{-1}j_H$ and
$p_Hr_h$ are the specified natural inclusion and projection with product
$1_{H_iG_i}$.

**Explicit rank-one inverse blocks.** Put $P=G_iH_i$, $V=H_iG_i$
at the common outside weight $\mu$, and write
$\eta_\mu:1_\mu\to H_iG_i$, $\varepsilon_\mu:G_iH_i\to1_\mu$
for the first adjunction and
$\eta'_\mu:1_\mu\to G_iH_i$, $\varepsilon'_\mu:H_iG_i\to1_\mu$
for the second. Let $\tau^{GG}$ be the native equal-color downward crossing
and $\tau^{HH}$ its twofold adjunction mate. Fix the native sideways mates by
$$T=(H_iG_i\varepsilon_\mu)(H_i\tau^{GG}H_i)(\eta_\mu G_iH_i),\qquad S=(G_iH_i\varepsilon'_\mu)(G_i\tau^{HH}G_i)(\eta'_\mu H_iG_i).$$
Their middle words are respectively $H_iG_iG_iH_i$ and
$G_iH_iH_iG_i$; the displayed final counits consume their rightmost
$G_iH_i$ and $H_iG_i$. Thus $T:P\to V$ and $S:V\to P$ are typed,
with degree $d_i(1-h)-2d_i+d_i(1+h)=0$. The source-crossing
component in the preceding rank-one matrix is $-T$. For $h\ge0$, its
identity columns are $C_k=x^k\eta_\mu$, and its identity rows are
$$R_k=\sum_{a+j=h-1-k}A_{\mu,j}\,\varepsilon'_\mu x^a,\qquad 0\le k<h,$$
where $a,j\ge0$. The matrix is $\rho=(-T,(C_k)_k):P\oplus D_h\to V$
and its specified inverse is $\sigma=(S,(R_k)_k):V\to P\oplus D_h$.
Impose both equations $\sigma\rho=1$ and $\rho\sigma=1$; in components
these say $-ST=1_P$, $R_kT=0$, $SC_k=0$, $R_kC_\ell=\delta_{k\ell}$
and $-TS+\sum_kC_kR_k=1_V$. For $h<0$, take
$C^-_k=x^k\eta'_\mu$ and
$$R^-_k=\sum_{a+j=-h-1-k}\mathsf H_{\mu,j}\,\varepsilon_\mu x^a,\qquad 0\le k<-h,$$
again with $a,j\ge0$. Now
$\rho=(-T,(R^-_k)_k):P\to V\oplus D_{-h}$ and
$\sigma=(S,(C^-_k)_k):V\oplus D_{-h}\to P$; impose
$\rho\sigma=1$, $\sigma\rho=1$. Equivalently $-TS=1_V$,
$TC^-_k=0$, $R^-_kS=0$, $R^-_kC^-_\ell=\delta_{k\ell}$ and
$-ST+\sum_kC^-_kR^-_k=1_P$. The shift summands $D_h,D_{-h}$ are
exactly those displayed above. The row degrees are respectively
$d_i(h-1-2k)$ and $-d_i(1+h+2k)$, opposite the column degrees, so every
matrix component is degree zero after the indicated shifts. Empty identity
sums at $h=0$ give the same inverse equations. These are imposed relations
in the presentation; a claim that the concrete flag bimodules satisfy them
still requires their local realization proof.

**Bubble series and slides.** The normalized far-left bubble series
$A_\mu(t),\mathsf H_\mu(t)$ have constant coefficient $1$ and satisfy
$A_\mu(t)\mathsf H_\mu(t)=1$. Genuine negative-degree bubbles vanish. The $A$
coefficient with index $m$ is the clockwise bubble with $-h-1+m$ dots when
this count is nonnegative, extended by formal inverse coefficients otherwise;
its degree is $2d_im$. The other family has dot count $h-1+\ell$ and degree
$2d_i\ell$. Impose the finite-coefficient slides verified on the monic flag
model: adjoining an $i$ root $z$ divides $A$ by $(1-zt)^2$ and multiplies
$\mathsf H$ by that factor; adjoining a spectator root $y$ of color $j\ne i$
multiplies $A$ by
$q_{ij}^{\mathrm{rev}}(y,t)=t^{-a_{ij}}Q_{ij}(t^{-1},y)/t_{ij}$, where $t_{ij}$
is the nonzero extremal coefficient, and divides $\mathsf H$ by it. Every
reciprocal coefficient is defined by the finite recursion with constant
coefficient $1$.

**Four oriented same-color equations.** The following notation specifies
actual local diagrams, all with color $i$. The two-crossing equations have
common outside weight $\mu$; the single curls have the adjacent region
weights specified individually below.
Read tangent directions in the page. Let $C_L,C_R$ be the cap arch
(two bottom endpoints and no top endpoints), whose tangent at its peak
points left or right, respectively. Their bottom arrows, from left to
right, are $(\downarrow,\uparrow)$ and
$(\uparrow,\downarrow)$. Let $U_L,U_R$ be the cup valley
(two top endpoints and no bottom endpoints), whose tangent at its trough
points left or right; their top arrows are
$(\uparrow,\downarrow)$ and $(\downarrow,\uparrow)$.
An exponent on $C$ or $U$ counts dots on its open arc. Let $B_{\mathrm{ccw}}^b$
and $B_{\mathrm{cw}}^b$ be the counterclockwise and clockwise bubbles
with literal dot count $b$, located to the right of the cap/cup in the outside
region of weight $\mu$. Their negative dot counts are exactly the fake
bubbles defined by the coefficient conventions above, not zero by convention.
Write $\eta_\mu:1_\mu\to H_iG_i$ and
$\varepsilon'_\mu:H_iG_i\to1_\mu$ for the first unit and second counit,
and $\eta'_\mu:1_\mu\to G_iH_i$, $\varepsilon_\mu:G_iH_i\to1_\mu$
for the second unit and first counit. Let $\tau^{HH}$ be the twofold
adjunction mate of the native equal-color downward crossing. Define
$$L_\mu=(H_i\varepsilon'_\mu)(\tau^{HH}G_i)(H_i\eta_\mu),\qquad R_\mu=(\varepsilon_\mu H_i)(G_i\tau^{HH})(\eta'_\mu H_i).$$
The first formula starts and ends at $H_i$ with input $\mu$; the second
starts and ends at $H_i$ with input $\mu-\alpha_i$. Thus both units and
counits in $L_\mu$ have degree $d_i(1-h)$, while those in $R_\mu$ have
degree $d_i(1+h)$. The crossing degree $-2d_i$ makes their degrees
$-2d_ih$ and $2d_ih$ respectively. Products in these formulas apply the
rightmost map first, with adjacent weights determined by composition.
Geometrically $L_\mu$ is an upward-strand curl with its loop bulging LEFT and
its left-adjacent region of weight $\mu$. This is an endomorphism of
$H_i$ at input $\mu$, and its bubble on the right-hand side is in the
left region $\mu$. Let $R_\mu$ be the upward-strand curl with its loop
bulging RIGHT and its right-adjacent region of weight $\mu$. Its left
region is $\mu-\alpha_i$, so it is an endomorphism of $H_i$ at input
$\mu-\alpha_i$, and its bubble is in the right region $\mu$.
Both have one native crossing and the two extremal turns of the loop.
Let $D_{\downarrow\uparrow}$ and $D_{\uparrow\downarrow}$ be the two
opposite crossing mates composed in the two orders on their indicated
straight boundaries, with common outside region $\mu$. Impose
$$L_\mu=\sum_{a+b=-1}x^aB_{\mathrm{ccw},\mu}^b,\qquad R_\mu=-\sum_{a+b=-1}x^aB_{\mathrm{cw},\mu}^b,$$
$$D_{\downarrow\uparrow}=-1_{\downarrow\uparrow}+\sum_{a+b+c=-2}C_L^aB_{\mathrm{cw},\mu}^bU_R^c,$$
$$D_{\uparrow\downarrow}=-1_{\uparrow\downarrow}+\sum_{a+b+c=-2}C_R^aB_{\mathrm{ccw},\mu}^bU_L^c.$$
Composition in the last two displays is top-to-bottom: $U$ first, then
the outside bubble, then $C$. The single-curl equations are upward-strand
endomorphism equations; their cup/cap forms are their specified adjunction
mates, not cap drawings with unspecified endpoint arrows. In every sum,
$a,c$ on open strands are nonnegative. The clockwise bubble with literal
$b$ dots is the $A_\mu$ coefficient of index $b+h+1$, and the
counterclockwise bubble is the $\mathsf H_\mu$ coefficient of index
$b-h+1$, where $h=\langle h_i,\mu\rangle$. Coefficients of negative index
are zero and the index-zero coefficient is one. The nonnegative coefficient
and open-dot indices make each sum finite. The opposite-crossing equations
have degree zero: their correction degrees are
$2d_i(1-h)+2d_i(a+b+c+h+1)=0$ and
$2d_i(1+h)+2d_i(a+b+c-h+1)=0$. The two curls have degrees
$-2d_ih$ and $2d_ih$ at their respective, different input weights.

The native single-crossing signs follow from $\kappa=-\tau$; two-crossing
signs are unchanged. The literal triple-dot sum is $-2$, not the compact
$-1$ printed in Webster's Figure 2: in the full positive-weight equation,
coefficient indices satisfy $f_1+f_2+f_3=h-1$ and the bubble has literal
count $b=-h-1+f_2$, giving $a+b+c=-2$; the negative-weight equation uses
$g_1+g_2+g_3=-h-1$ and $b=h-1+g_2$, giving the same value. Reflection
exchanges the two bubble orientations and preserves region weights. The
single-curl coefficient sums instead have total $h$ or $-h$, yielding
literal $a+b=-1$. At $h=0$ the triple sums are empty and the single
curls are respectively $+1$ and $-1$ on their specified shifted input
weights. At the $h=1$, $p(u)=u$ vacuum, $H_iG_i=k$, $G_iH_i=0$,
$A_\mu=1$ and the only surviving clockwise bubble has $b=-2$; thus the
first cancellation is $0=-1_k+1_k$, with no degree or vacuum contradiction.

**Distinct-color crossing mates.** For $j\ne i$, the two sideways crossings, defined as the two
adjunction mates of the downward crossing, cancel in the two orders with the
nonzero scalars $t_{ij}$ and $t_{ji}$; scale the reverse mate by the
corresponding inverse to obtain the mixed isomorphism
$H_iG_j\cong G_jH_i$, commuting with the $j$ dot.

**Status of the relations.** These equations are relations of this proof-tool
category. Their consistency and homogeneous realization are established by
the polynomial flag model
([[lem-minimal-parabolic-polynomial-flag-model-realizes-the-graded-diagram-relations]]),
rather than assumed for the actual cyclotomic induction/restriction action; no
claim about the latter is made here. This definition uses no choice: it is a
presentation by generators and homogeneous equations, and every sl(2) infinite
family appearing in the matrix and bubble clauses is a finite coefficient
recursion from a constant coefficient $1$.
items.strategy: This is a presentation by generators and homogeneous equations. Check weighted homogeneity of every downward relation using $\deg x_j=2d_j$ and $\deg\tau_{jk}=-b_{jk}$; the global source substitution changes every crossing sign and preserves $Q$. Check the two cup/cap degrees at adjacent weights, giving degree-zero triangle composites and the symmetric identity shifts in both branches of the rank-one matrix. Interpret all fake bubbles and reciprocal slide coefficients by the finite recursion from constant coefficient1, so no analytic series or inverse dot occurs. The local polynomial flag model realizes these equations with normalized $H_i$, shifted spectator flags, explicit dual monic power bases and the actual rank-one inverse blocks, proving consistency. This last well-definedness result is listed in justified_by, while its proof depends on the present definition; it is not a logical dependency of the definition.

items.title: Mixed relations, local nilpotence and weights give the integrable quantum action
items.statement:
Let $V=\bigoplus_{\mu\in P}V_\mu$ be a label-weight-graded $\mathbb Q(q)$-vector
space with toral operators $K_h$ ($h\in P^\vee$) acting on $V_\mu$ by
$q^{\langle\mu,h\rangle}$, and operators $E_i,F_i$ of weights
$\alpha_i,-\alpha_i$ mapping $V_\mu$ to $V_{\mu+\alpha_i}$ and
$V_{\mu-\alpha_i}$. Assume the toral conjugation and mixed relations, and local
nilpotence of each $E_i$ and $F_i$; vectors have finite label support. Then
these operators uniquely define an integrable type-one
$U_q(\mathfrak g)$-module structure on $V$ for EVERY real symmetrizable Cartan
datum. Every vector has a finite rank-one $U_i$ orbit and the admissible
Kashiwara $i$-string decomposition applies. Finite weight spaces do not imply
finite-dimensional full-$\mathfrak g$ orbits; no such conclusion is asserted.
items.strategy:
**Proof technique:** finite rank-one reductions: enclose each vector in a finite-dimensional rank-one module, use the rank-one adjoint action on a Hom space to turn $F_j$ into a highest vector, bound its string by the divided-power commutation formula, and read the Serre sum off the surviving coefficient.

1.1 Finite rank-one orbits. Fix $i$ and $v\in V$. Then $W:=\operatorname{span}\{F_i^aE_i^bK_i^cv:a,b\ge0,\ c\in\mathbb Z\}$ is a finite-dimensional $A_i$-stable subspace, where $A_i$ is the algebra generated by $E_i,F_i,K_i^{\pm1}$: the toral operator $K_i$ acts diagonally on the finitely many nonzero label components of $v$, so the vectors $K_i^cv$ span a finite-dimensional subspace; by [A3] there is $B$ with $E_i^bv=0$ for $b\ge B$; the mixed relation of [A2] rewrites any word in $E_i,F_i$ as a linear combination of words $F_i^aE_i^b$ with coefficients in the algebra generated by $K_i$; and one may choose finitely many $K_i^cv$ spanning the toral orbit and use local nilpotence of $F_i$ on their finitely many $E_i^b$-images to bound $a$. The span of the resulting finite set is stable under $E_i,F_i,K_i^{\pm1}$. [A1, A2, A3]

2.1 The second finite module. Fix $i\ne j$ and set $W':=\operatorname{span}\{F_i^aE_i^bK_i^cF_jw:w\in W,\ a,b\ge0,\ c\in\mathbb Z\}$. Since $W$ is finite-dimensional, step 1.1 applied to each of the finitely many vectors $F_jw$ exhibits $W'$ as a finite union of finite-dimensional $A_i$-stable subspaces; hence $W'$ is a finite-dimensional $A_i$-stable subspace of $V$ containing $F_jW$. [step 1.1, A1, A2, A3]

3.1 The rank-one adjoint module. On the finite-dimensional space $\operatorname{Hom}(W,W')$ define operators by $\mathrm{Ad}(K_i)(T)=K_iTK_i^{-1}$, $\mathrm{Ad}(E_i)(T)=(E_iT-TE_i)K_i$ and $\mathrm{Ad}(F_i)(T)=F_iT-K_iTK_i^{-1}F_i$. Substituting these formulas, using $K_iE_i=q_i^2E_iK_i$, $K_iF_i=q_i^{-2}F_iK_i$ and $E_iF_i-F_iE_i=(K_i-K_i^{-1})/(q_i-q_i^{-1})$ on $W,W^{\prime}$, gives $\mathrm{Ad}(K_i)\mathrm{Ad}(E_i)\mathrm{Ad}(K_i)^{-1}=q_i^2\mathrm{Ad}(E_i)$, $\mathrm{Ad}(K_i)\mathrm{Ad}(F_i)\mathrm{Ad}(K_i)^{-1}=q_i^{-2}\mathrm{Ad}(F_i)$ and $[\mathrm{Ad}(E_i),\mathrm{Ad}(F_i)]=(\mathrm{Ad}(K_i)-\mathrm{Ad}(K_i)^{-1})/(q_i-q_i^{-1})$. Thus these formulas give a rank-one module directly. Moreover $\mathrm{Ad}(K_i)$ is diagonalizable because $K_i$ acts diagonally on $W$ and $W'$, and $\mathrm{Ad}(E_i),\mathrm{Ad}(F_i)$ are locally nilpotent: $\mathrm{Ad}(E_i)$ raises and $\mathrm{Ad}(F_i)$ lowers the $\mathrm{Ad}(K_i)$-weight by $2$, the weights of $\operatorname{Hom}(W,W')$ form a finite set, and decomposing any $T$ into weight components each orbit is supported on distinct weights and hence terminates. [A1, A2, step 2.1]

4.1 $F_j$ is a highest vector of weight $m$. Since $F_jW\subseteq W'$, the restriction $T:=F_j|_W$ lies in $\operatorname{Hom}(W,W')$. By [A2], $E_iF_j=F_jE_i$ for $i\ne j$, so $\mathrm{Ad}(E_i)(T)=(E_iT-TE_i)K_i=0$; and by [A1], $\mathrm{Ad}(K_i)(T)=K_iF_jK_i^{-1}=q_i^{-a_{ij}}T$, because $\langle\alpha_j,d_ih_i\rangle=d_ia_{ij}$. Put $m:=-a_{ij}\ge0$, the off-diagonal Cartan entries being nonpositive. Thus $T$ is annihilated by $\mathrm{Ad}(E_i)$ and has $\mathrm{Ad}(K_i)$-weight $q_i^m$ with $m\ge0$. [A1, A2, step 3.1]

5.1 The rank-one string bound. Assume $T\ne0$. In the rank-one module $\operatorname{Hom}(W,W')$ of steps 3.1-4.1 let $t\ge1$ be minimal with $\mathrm{Ad}(F_i)^tT=0$; it exists by the local nilpotence of step 3.1. For $b\ge1$ the divided-power formula of [F3] gives $\mathrm{Ad}(E_i)\mathrm{Ad}(F_i)^{(b)}(T)=\mathrm{Ad}(F_i)^{(b-1)}\Theta_{i,b}(T)$, and $\Theta_{i,b}$ acts on $T$ by the scalar $\frac{1}{q_i^b-q_i^{-b}}\sum_{s=0}^{b-1}(q_i^{m-2s}-q_i^{-m+2s})=\frac{q_i^{m-b+1}-q_i^{-m+b-1}}{q_i-q_i^{-1}}=[m-b+1]_i$, by summing the two geometric progressions. Taking $b=t$ and using $\mathrm{Ad}(F_i)^tT=0$ together with $\mathrm{Ad}(F_i)^{(t-1)}T=[t-1]_i!^{-1}\mathrm{Ad}(F_i)^{t-1}T\ne0$ gives $[m-t+1]_i=0$, hence $m-t+1=0$ by [F2], that is $t=m+1$; therefore $\mathrm{Ad}(F_i)^{m+1}T=0$. [F2, F3, step 4.1]

6.1 The Serre sum. By induction on $n\ge0$, using $\mathrm{Ad}(K_i)(T)=q_i^mT$ and the Pascal recurrence of [F4], the powers of the adjoint action expand as $\mathrm{Ad}(F_i)^n(T)=\sum_{r=0}^{n}(-1)^rq_i^{r(m-n+1)}\binom{n}{r}_iF_i^{n-r}TF_i^r$: the case $n=0$ is clear, and applying $\mathrm{Ad}(F_i)$ to the formula for $n$, conjugating $K_iF_i^{n-r}TF_i^rK_i^{-1}=q_i^{m-2n}F_i^{n-r}TF_i^r$ and comparing the coefficient of $F_i^{n+1-r}TF_i^r$ uses exactly $C_{n+1,r}=q_i^rC_{n,r}+q_i^{r-n-1}C_{n,r-1}$, the second form of [F4]. At $n=m+1=1-a_{ij}$ every Laurent exponent $r(m-n+1)$ is zero, so step 5.1 gives $\sum_{r=0}^{1-a_{ij}}(-1)^r\binom{1-a_{ij}}{r}_iF_i^{1-a_{ij}-r}F_jF_i^r=0$ on $W$. Since every $v\in V$ lies in such a $W$ by step 1.1, the negative Serre relation holds as an operator on all of $V$. [F4, step 1.1, step 5.1]

7.1 The positive Serre relation. Put $E_i':=F_i$, $F_i':=E_i$ and $K_h':=K_{-h}$ for all $i$ and $h$. The primed data again satisfies the toral, toral-action, mixed and local-nilpotence hypotheses [A1]-[A3]: for instance $K_h'E_i'K_h'^{-1}=K_{-h}F_iK_h=q^{\langle\alpha_i,h\rangle}F_i=q^{\langle\alpha_i,h\rangle}E_i'$, while $E_i'F_i'-F_i'E_i'=F_iE_i-E_iF_i=-(K_i-K_i^{-1})/(q_i-q_i^{-1})=(K_i'-K_i'^{-1})/(q_i-q_i^{-1})$. Applying steps 1.1-6.1 to the primed data gives $\sum_{r}(-1)^r\binom{1-a_{ij}}{r}_iE_i^{1-a_{ij}-r}E_jE_i^r=0$ on $V$, which is the positive Serre relation for the original data. [A1, A2, A3, step 6.1]

8.1 Conclusion. By [A1]-[A3] the operators satisfy all the defining relations of $U_q(\mathfrak g)$: the toral and toral-action relations, the mixed commutators, and both Serre families by steps 6.1 and 7.1. Hence the universal property [F1] equips $V$ with a $U_q(\mathfrak g)$-module structure; it is unique because $U_q(\mathfrak g)$ is generated by these operators, and it is a chosen $P$-graded type-one weight module by construction. Local nilpotence is exactly [A3], so the module is integrable, and by [F5] the admissible $i$-string decomposition applies to every vector; step 1.1 supplies the finite rank-one $U_i$ orbit. No finite-dimensionality of the full weight spaces is asserted or used. [A3, F1, F5, step 1.1, step 6.1, step 7.1] ∎

items.title: Cyclotomic KLR induction and restriction functors
items.statement:
Use the standard graded cyclotomic quotient of
[[def-cyclotomic-klr-quotient-at-a-dominant-weight]], and keep the conventions
fixed there: the cyclotomic relation is imposed on the FIRST strand and
cyclotomic induction appends strands on the RIGHT. Fix $\beta\in Q_+$ and a
color $i$; put
$$A:=R^\Lambda(\beta),\qquad B:=R^\Lambda(\beta+\alpha_i),\qquad e:=e(\beta,i),$$
where $e(\beta,i)=\sum_{\nu\in I^\beta}e(\nu i)\in R(\beta+\alpha_i)$ is the
idempotent of [[def-quiver-hecke-klr-algebra-for-a-symmetrizable-cartan-datum]]
supported on the sequences ending in $i$.

**The right-append corner homomorphism.** Right append defines a
$k$-algebra homomorphism
$$\iota_i:A\longrightarrow eBe,\qquad 1_A\longmapsto e,\quad e(\nu)\longmapsto e(\nu i),\quad x_a\longmapsto x_a,\quad \tau_a\longmapsto\tau_a ,$$
sending each old dot or crossing to the same-named generator at the same
position in the first $|\beta|$ strands of $R^\Lambda(\beta+\alpha_i)$ and
each old idempotent to the longer idempotent obtained by appending $i$. It is
a graded homomorphism of degree zero: each generic relation (1)-(7) of
[[def-quiver-hecke-klr-algebra-for-a-symmetrizable-cartan-datum]] is preserved
under right append, and the first-strand cyclotomic generator of $A$ maps to
the first-strand cyclotomic generator of $B$, so the cyclotomic relation is
preserved and $\iota_i$ is well defined on the quotient. The unit is sent to
the corner unit $e$, not to a global unit of $B$; it is **not** asserted that
$\iota_i$ is injective, and $e$ is allowed to be zero.

**The functors.** On graded left modules define
$$F_i^{\mathrm{basic}}(M):=Be\otimes_A M,\qquad E_i^{\mathrm{basic}}(N):=eN,$$
the tensor over the graded balanced tensor product of
[[def-graded-balanced-tensor-product-and-homogeneous-hom]] and the idempotent
restriction of the graded $B$-module $N$
([[def-graded-ring-module-bimodule-and-internal-shift]]). Both are additive
$k$-linear functors between the graded module categories, they preserve
degree-zero maps, and they extend to direct sums over the root degrees
$\beta\in Q_+$.

**Adjunction, weights and shifts.** Evaluation at $e$ identifies
$\operatorname{HOM}_B(Be,N)$ with $eN$ by the degree-zero tensor--Hom
adjunction, giving $F_i^{\mathrm{basic}}\dashv E_i^{\mathrm{basic}}$ with its
actual grading. The functor $F_i^{\mathrm{basic}}$ increases ROOT degree by
$\alpha_i$, taking modules at root $\beta$ to modules at root
$\beta+\alpha_i$, and decreases the module weight $\Lambda-\beta$ by
$\alpha_i$; restriction does the reverse. Both composites are endofunctors at
a fixed root degree. Grading shifts satisfy
$F_i^{\mathrm{basic}}(M\{r\})\cong F_i^{\mathrm{basic}}(M)\{r\}$ and
$E_i^{\mathrm{basic}}(N\{r\})\cong E_i^{\mathrm{basic}}(N)\{r\}$, using the
internal shifts of [[def-graded-ring-module-bimodule-and-internal-shift]].

**Ungraded monic deformations.** For a general monic
specialization $a_j(u)$ the quotient $R^\Lambda_a(\beta)$ of
[[def-cyclotomic-klr-quotient-at-a-dominant-weight]] carries no grading, and
the same formulas define the ungraded functors $F_i^{\mathrm{basic}}$ and
$E_i^{\mathrm{basic}}$; no graded statement is asserted on that branch.

**Status of further structure.** Exactness, preservation of projectives and a
shifted second adjunction are theorems below, not part of this definition; in
particular no unshifted right adjunction $E_i^{\mathrm{basic}}\dashv
F_i^{\mathrm{basic}}$ is asserted here, and the explicit shift of the second
adjunction is supplied by the coherent-biadjunction lemma of this page. This
definition uses no choice.
items.strategy: Each generic generator relation is preserved in the corner, and the first-strand cyclotomic generator maps into the longer ideal. This gives a homomorphism with unit image $e$, not a global-unit inclusion. For example $\lambda_i=1$, $\beta=\alpha_i$ has $A=k$, $B=0$, so the corner homomorphism and induction are zero. Evaluation at $e$ identifies $\operatorname{HOM}_B(Be,N)$ with $eN$, proving the ordinary adjunction with its actual grading. Finite balanced tensors give additivity/shift compatibility. No unshifted second adjunction is assumed; its explicit shift is supplied by the coherent-adjunction lemma.

items.title: Cyclotomic dot annihilators, finite-dimensional blocks, and finite root strings
items.statement:
Let $k$ be any field and let $Q$ satisfy (Q1)-(Q4) for a real symmetrizable
Cartan datum with finite color set. For monic $a_j(u)\in k[u]$ of degree
$\lambda_j\ge0$, impose $a_{\nu_1}(x_1)e(\nu)=0$ and write $R^a(\beta)$ for the
resulting ordinary quotient. Then: every dot has a scalar-coefficient monic
annihilator in each fixed block; every $R^a(\beta)$ is finite dimensional over
$k$; and, for fixed $\beta$ and $i$, $R^a(\beta+m\alpha_i)=0$ for all
sufficiently large $m$. Thus right-append induction has finite $i$-strings. In
the standard homogeneous specialization $a_j(u)=u^{\lambda_j}$, every dot is
nilpotent and these are statements about the induced graded algebra and graded
functors. For an inhomogeneous monic specialization the assertions are
ungraded; no graded highest-weight Grothendieck identification is included.

items.title: Generic KLR induction and restriction: mixed relations and the opposite-end exact sequence
items.statement:
Let $R=\bigoplus_\beta R(\beta)$ be a KLR algebra on a symmetrizable Cartan datum
with no imaginary simple roots
([[def-quiver-hecke-klr-algebra-for-a-symmetrizable-cartan-datum]]) and let
$E_i$ denote restriction $e(\beta,i)(-)$ and $F_i$, $\bar F_i$ the right-append
and left-append inductions of [[def-klr-induction-and-restriction-bimodules]]
(so that $\bar F_i(M)=R(\beta+\alpha_i)e(i,\beta)\otimes_{R(\beta)}M$ with
$e(i,\beta)=\sum_{\nu\in I^\beta}e(i\ast\nu)$). Let $t_i$ be an indeterminate of
degree $(\alpha_i\mid\alpha_i)=2d_i$. Then:

(a) for $i\ne j$ there are natural isomorphisms
$E_iF_j\cong q^{-(\alpha_i\mid\alpha_j)}F_jE_i$ and
$\bar F_jE_i\cong E_i\bar F_j$;

(b) for $i=j$ there is a natural isomorphism
$E_iF_i\cong q^{-(\alpha_i\mid\alpha_i)}F_iE_i\oplus(\mathrm{Id}\otimes_kk[t_i])$,
where $(\mathrm{Id}\otimes_kk[t_i])(M)=M\otimes_kk[t_i]$ with $t_i$ homogeneous
of degree $2d_i$;

(c) the opposite-end corner comparison gives a functorial exact sequence in
$\mathrm{Mod}(R(\beta))$
$$0\longrightarrow \bar F_iE_iM\longrightarrow E_i\bar F_iM\longrightarrow q^{-(\alpha_i\mid\beta)}M\otimes_kk[t_i]\longrightarrow 0,$$
where $\otimes_kk[t_i]$ is understood in the graded sense. For $n\ge1$, the underlying uncolored bimodules have the exact sequence
$0\to R(n)\otimes_{R_1(n-1)}R_1(n)\to R(n+1)\to R(n)\otimes_kk^I[t]\to0$,
where $k^I=\bigoplus_{j\in I}k\epsilon_j$ retains the transferred strand color,
and the right $R(n)$ action is through the shift embedding $\xi_n$.
The quotient grading is the degree of the full transfer word on each labeled
corner; its fixed-color $i$ corner is the shifted polynomial term of (c). All shifts are computed in the fixed grading of
[[def-klr-grading-and-diagrammatic-composition]]; the functors are exact
([[thm-klr-induction-and-restriction-are-biadjoint-and-preserve-projectives]]).
items.strategy:
**Proof technique:** compare PBW bases for the two same-end double cosets and for the opposite-end overlap, then pass to the correct colored corners and tensor only a right-split exact sequence.

1.1 Conventions and PBW coordinates. Put $\kappa_a=-\tau_a$ for every color pair, so $\kappa_w=(-1)^{\ell(w)}\tau_w$ has the same degree and is a PBW basis with the source dot and braid signs. For $n\ge1$, embed $R(n)$ on positions $1,\ldots,n$ and $R_1(n)=\xi_nR(n)$ on positions $2,\ldots,n+1$; their overlap is $R_1(n-1)$ on positions $2,\ldots,n$. Write $k^I=\bigoplus_{j\in I}k\epsilon_j$ for the color algebra. Choosing reduced words adapted to the cosets gives the left PBW decomposition $R(n+1)=\bigoplus_{a=1}^{n+1}R(n,1)\kappa_n\cdots\kappa_a$ and the right PBW decomposition $R(n+1)=\bigoplus_{a=1}^{n+1}\kappa_a\cdots\kappa_n(k^I[x_{n+1}]\otimes_kR(n))$, where the product for $a=n+1$ is $1$. These are labelled decompositions: polynomial and idempotent coefficients keep the transferred color, and crossing degrees are summed on the actual word. PBW independence follows by using those reduced coset words followed by a reduced word in $S_n$; the resulting products have additive lengths and are precisely the chosen PBW basis. [F1, F2, algebra]

1.2 The empty-word case. At $\beta=0$ the KLR presentation gives $R(0)=k$ and $R(\alpha_j)=k[x_1]e(j)$ with $\deg x_1=2d_j$. The empty word has no last strand, so its $E_i$-restriction is zero on the weight-graded category, without introducing a negative-height algebra. Both append inductions of a graded $k$-module $M$ are $k[x_1]e(j)\otimes_kM$. Orthogonality of $e(i),e(j)$ gives $E_iF_jM=E_i\bar F_jM=0$ for $i\ne j$, whereas $E_iF_iM=E_i\bar F_iM\cong M\otimes_kk[t_i]$ by $x_1^a\otimes m\mapsto m\otimes t_i^a$, naturally and in degree zero. Thus (a) is zero-to-zero, (b) has precisely the polynomial summand with coefficient $1$, and (c) is $0\to0\to M\otimes_kk[t_i]\xrightarrow{\mathrm{id}}M\otimes_kk[t_i]\to0$, since $(\alpha_i\mid0)=0$. The uncolored overlap formula involving $R_1(n-1)$ below is used only for $n\ge1$. [F2, F3, algebra]

2.1 The same-end double cosets. For $n\ge1$ define $T:R(n)\otimes_{R(n-1)}R(n)\to R(n+1)$ by $x\otimes y\mapsto x\kappa_ny$, with both outer algebras embedded on the first $n$ positions. It is balanced because $\kappa_n$ commutes with the generators on positions $1,\ldots,n-1$. Decompose the first factor as the right $R(n-1)$-module $\bigoplus_{a=1}^n\kappa_a\cdots\kappa_{n-1}(k^I[x_n]\otimes_kR(n-1))$. For a polynomial/color coefficient $f(x_n)$, the dot move gives $f(x_n)\kappa_n=\kappa_nf(x_{n+1})+c$, where $c$ lies in the polynomial/idempotent algebra on the first $n+1$ positions and its last-color projector equals its adjacent-color projector; consequently $\kappa_a\cdots\kappa_{n-1}c\,y$ lies in $R(n,1)$. Modulo $R(n,1)$ the image is therefore exactly $\kappa_a\cdots\kappa_nf(x_{n+1})y$. These are the right PBW cosets $a=1,\ldots,n$, bijectively, with coefficient $1$, so the induced quotient map is an isomorphism. Inclusion of $R(n,1)$ then gives the actual bimodule isomorphism $T\oplus\mathrm{incl}:R(n)\otimes_{R(n-1)}R(n)\oplus R(n,1)\to R(n+1)$: injectivity and surjectivity follow by first passing to the quotient and then to the included summand. This retains all nonidentity cosets, rather than discarding cosets $a>1$. [step 1.1, F2, algebra]

2.2 The opposite-end overlap map. For $n\ge1$, multiplication defines a balanced $(R(n),R_1(n))$-bimodule map $U:R(n)\otimes_{R_1(n-1)}R_1(n)\to R(n+1)$, $x\otimes y\mapsto xy$. The PBW decomposition in the last $n$ positions is $R_1(n)=\bigoplus_{a=2}^{n+1}(R_1(n-1)\otimes_kk^I[x_{n+1}])\kappa_n\cdots\kappa_a$. Tensoring this displayed free decomposition identifies the domain of $U$ with $\bigoplus_{a=2}^{n+1}R(n,1)\kappa_n\cdots\kappa_a$. Multiplication maps each basis element to the identically named PBW element, so $U$ is injective and its image $J$ is exactly those cosets. Using the opposite PBW decomposition gives also $J=\bigoplus_{a=0}^{n-1}\kappa_a\cdots\kappa_1R(1,n)$, where $a=0$ is the empty product. Thus $J$ is the overlap bimodule, not a two-sided ideal, and the quotient has the sole remaining transfer coset $R(n,1)\kappa_n\cdots\kappa_1$, equivalently $\kappa_n\cdots\kappa_1R(1,n)$. [step 1.1, F1, F2, algebra]

3.1 Correct same-end colored kernels. For an input weight $\beta$ set $\delta=\beta-\alpha_i$ and $\gamma=\delta+\alpha_j$. When $\delta\in Q_+$, the kernel of $E_iF_j$ is $e(\gamma,i)R(\beta+\alpha_j)e(\beta,j)$, an $(R(\gamma),R(\beta))$-bimodule. Cutting the isomorphism of step 2.1 by these idempotents gives the image under $T$ of $R(\gamma)e(\delta,j)\otimes_{R(\delta)}e(\delta,i)R(\beta)$, the kernel of $F_jE_i$. The factors project onto the two colors interchanged by $\kappa_n$, so its degree is exactly $-b_{ij}$, and the image is the domain shifted by $-b_{ij}$. If $\delta\notin Q_+$, $E_i$ has zero restriction on the input weight because no word of weight $\beta$ ends in $i$; the transfer summand is zero, without writing any algebra at a negative weight. For $i\ne j$ the one-strand-enlarged word then also has no $i$ endpoint, so $E_iF_j$ is zero. The other summand $R(n,1)$ preserves the last color, so it vanishes exactly for $i\ne j$; for $i=j$ its corner is $R(\beta)\otimes_kk[t_i]$, with $\deg t_i=2d_i$. Hence the bimodule maps give (a)'s same-end isomorphism and (b), with coefficient $1$ on the polynomial summand. Tensoring an actual bimodule isomorphism with any graded input module preserves it; no exactness or flatness assumption is needed for this passage. [step 2.1, F2, F3, algebra]

3.2 The quotient and its right splitting. Put $w=\kappa_n\cdots\kappa_1$. Move a dot or crossing along $w$ by the local relations. Modulo $J$ these moves give $x_aw=w x_{a+1}$ for $1\le a\le n$, $x_{n+1}w=w x_1$, and $\kappa_aw=w\kappa_{a+1}$ for $1\le a<n$. Dot corrections remove one crossing and braid corrections remove the three-crossing braid block; in each case the surviving permutation fails to transfer the first endpoint all the way to the last endpoint, so its PBW coset is among $a=2,\ldots,n+1$ and lies in $J$. Idempotents simply follow the same cyclic permutation. These generator identities prove $a f(x_{n+1})w=w\xi_n(a)f(x_1)$ in the quotient. Taking the coefficient of $w$ therefore identifies the underlying bimodule quotient with $R(n)\otimes_kk^I[t]$, the right $R(n)$ action being through $\xi_n$, and both indicated endpoint dots becoming $t$. The color algebra is retained because the transferred endpoint can have any color. Its right PBW expression $w(k^I[x_1]\otimes_kR_1(n))$ provides a right $R_1(n)$-linear section of the quotient map by choosing those same PBW representatives. It need not be a bimodule section. Hence the sequence defined by $U$ and this coefficient map is right-split before any tensoring. [step 2.2, F2, algebra]

4.1 Opposite-end colored kernels and degrees. With $\delta,\gamma$ as in step 3.1 and $\delta\in Q_+$, the kernel of $E_i\bar F_j$ is $e(\gamma,i)R(\beta+\alpha_j)e(j,\beta)$, with right $R(\beta)$ action through $\xi_n$. Cutting $U$ identifies its overlap submodule with $R(\gamma)e(j,\delta)\otimes_{R(\delta)}e(\delta,i)R(\beta)$, the kernel of $\bar F_jE_i$, by the plain multiplication map; this map adds no crossing and has degree zero. The quotient transfer word $w$ takes bottom $(j,\nu)$ to top $(\nu,j)$, so this quotient corner vanishes for $i\ne j$ and gives the unshifted opposite-end isomorphism in (a). For $i=j$ and $\nu$ of weight $\beta$, $w e(i,\nu)$ has degree $-\sum_a b_{i\nu_a}=-(\alpha_i\mid\beta)$. Thus the quotient corner is $q^{-(\alpha_i\mid\beta)}R(\beta)\otimes_kk[t_i]$, with the label $i$ fixed and $\deg t_i=2d_i$. The right section in step 3.2 respects these color projectors and this degree shift, so the colored sequence is split as right $R(\beta)$-modules. Tensoring with any graded $M$ retains its injective first map and exact quotient and gives precisely (c), functorially, with the stated shift. If $\delta\notin Q_+$ the overlap corner is zero; at $\beta=0$ this agrees with step 1.2. [step 3.1, step 2.2, step 3.2, F3, algebra]

5.1 Conclusion. Steps 1.2 and 3.1 establish the same-end mixed isomorphisms, and step 4.1 establishes the opposite-end isomorphism and exact sequence for every weight. All maps are the explicit homogeneous PBW corner maps above; the opposite-end sequence is right-split before tensoring, and the uncolored expression retains its transferred-color labels and uses $n\ge1$. The dots, crossing signs and shifts are those of the fixed native grading, with the source normalization $\kappa=-\tau$ affecting only unit PBW coefficients. No quotient flatness, uniform shift for all labelled cosets, or negative-height algebra is assumed. [step 1.2, step 3.1, step 4.1] ∎

items.title: The minimal-parabolic polynomial flag model realizes the graded diagram relations
items.statement:
Fix a color $i$ and the formal proof category of
[[def-minimal-parabolic-klr-diagram-proof-category]], on a symmetrizable real
Cartan datum with finite index set and arbitrary field $k$. Use the native KLR
parameters of
[[def-quiver-hecke-klr-algebra-for-a-symmetrizable-cartan-datum]], degrees of
[[def-klr-grading-and-diagrammatic-composition]], the PBW convention of
[[thm-klr-pbw-basis-theorem]], and the nil-Hecke matrix/idempotent convention
of [[def-divided-power-klr-idempotents-and-projectives]]. Then the polynomial
flag construction described below realizes all the defining graded diagram
relations of that formal category, including its rank-one cross/cap,
bubble-slide/inversion and mixed-color cup/cap relations; it asserts a
representation of the formal proof category, not faithfulness or a cyclotomic
quotient identification.

**The model.** Choose a color order with $i$ last. For spectator alphabets
$Y_j$ of sizes $m_j$ ($j\ne i$) put $C=\bigotimes_{j\ne i}k[Y_j]^{S_{m_j}}$,
$r=m_i$, $A_{ij}=-a_{ij}$,
$t_{ij}=[u^{A_{ij}}]Q_{ij}(u,v)\in k^\times$,
$q_{ij}=Q_{ij}/t_{ij}$, and choose a monic framing polynomial $a_i(u)$ of
degree $\lambda_i$; initially its coefficients have their universal homogeneous
degrees, so all formulas are graded, and the standard specialization is
$a_i(u)=u^{\lambda_i}$. Set
$$p_m(u)=a_i(u)\prod_{j\ne i}\prod_{y\in Y_j}q_{ij}(u,y),\qquad N=\lambda_i+\sum_{j\ne i}A_{ij}m_j,\qquad h_m=N-2r,$$
and $c_r(u)=u^r-e_1u^{r-1}+\cdots+(-1)^re_r$. The vertex ring $L_m$ is the
monic factor ring for $p_m=c_rb_{N-r}$, equivalently $C[e_1,\ldots,e_r]$ modulo
all coefficients beyond degree $N-r$ of the monic expansion $p_m/c_r$; it is
finite free over $C$ of rank $\binom Nr$ and is zero for $r>N$. Its $i$ flag is
$B_m=L_m[z]/b_{N-r}(z)$, free of rank $N-r$ over $L_m$ and rank $r+1$ over
$L_{m+i}$, with the target root alphabet obtained by adjoining $z$. The
underlying spectator flag is $C_m^j=L_m[y]$; its target action appends $y$ to
$Y_j$ and replaces $p_m$ by $p_mq_{ij}(u,y)$.

**The shifts and generators.** Every downward generator carries the ordered
shift $s_j(m)=-2d_jm_j+\sum_{\ell>j}(-b_{j\ell})m_\ell$. Thus
$G_i=F_i^{\mathrm{basic}}$ is the $B_m\{-2d_ir\}$ tensor functor; $G_j$ for
$j\ne i$ is the $C_m^j\{s_j(m)\}$ tensor functor. The basic reversed $i$ flag
is $E_i^{\mathrm{basic}}=B_m\otimes_{L_{m+i}}-$ without a shift, whereas the
formal upward generator at INPUT vertex $m$ is
$H_i(m)=E_i^{\mathrm{basic}}(m)\{-d_i(1+h_m)\}$. These are distinct
conventions. The basic flags have degree-zero
$F_i^{\mathrm{basic}}\dashv E_i^{\mathrm{basic}}$ and
$E_i^{\mathrm{basic}}\{t_i(m)\}\dashv F_i^{\mathrm{basic}}$, where
$t_i(m)=-2d_i(h_m-1)$. At vertex $m$ the formal first unit and second cap have
degree $d_i(1-h_m)$, and the formal first cap and second unit have degree
$d_i(1+h_m)$.

**The four maps and the Casimir.** All four maps are the explicit dual-basis
maps of the two monic coefficient forms on $B_m$: $\tau_{\mathrm{old}}:B_m\to
L_m$ extracts $z^{N-r-1}$ and has degree $-2d_i(N-r-1)$;
$\tau_{\mathrm{new}}:B_m\to L_{m+i}$ extracts $z^r$ and has degree $-2d_ir$.
The first cap is $b_1\otimes b_2\mapsto\tau_{\mathrm{new}}(b_1b_2)$ and the
first cup is its dual-power-basis Casimir; the second cap and cup use
$\tau_{\mathrm{old}}$. For a monic polynomial $f$ their Casimir is the
polynomial kernel $K_f(X,Y)=(f(X)-f(Y))/(X-Y)$ in the two-root quotient.

**Crossings, colors and bubbles.** Source crossings are
$\kappa=-\tau_{\mathrm{native}}$ for EVERY color pair. Source equal-color
operators are $(s-1)/(X-Y)$; source unequal operators are the switch/quotient
in the increasing-color direction and switch times $Q$ in the reverse
direction. Thus native operators are their negatives, and both actual crossing
degrees are $-b_{jk}$ with the ordered shifts above. On the $i,j$ pair the
successive underlying rings are
$D_1=L_m[y,z]/(b(z)q_{ij}(z,y))$ and $D_0=L_m[y,z]/b(z)$, with source maps
$\pi:D_1\to D_0$ and $f\mapsto Q_{ij}(z,y)f:D_0\to D_1$; their normalized
opposite-sideways composites have the scalars $t_{ij}$ and $t_{ji}$, and in the
NE/SW-$i$, NW/SE-$j$ source orientation the double-mate ratio is
$t_{ji}/t_{ij}$. Native minus signs leave the two-crossing scalars and the
ratio unchanged. The basic isomorphism $E_iG_j\cong(G_jE_i)\{-b_{ij}\}$ holds,
and the normalized formal $H_iG_j\cong G_jH_i$ is unshifted.

**Realized equations.** The canonical rank-one $\rho$ and its inverse, the
same-color cross/cap equations, the bubble series
$\Phi_i(u)=p_m(u)/c_r(u)^2$ and its reciprocal, and the finite-coefficient
bubble-slide identities are realized by the stated polynomial maps. In
particular the normalized positive $h$ identity columns have degrees
$d_i(1-h+2k)$ for $0\le k<h$, and the negative branch uses the inverse
crossing plus the dot/cap rows. All polynomial pairings and relations persist
after arbitrary monic coefficient specialization as UNGRADED identities; such
a specialization does not assert nilpotence, a homogeneous trace degree, or a
highest-weight $K_0$ claim. No geometry, characteristic restriction, or
one-dimensional-Hom hypothesis is imposed.
items.strategy:
**Proof technique:** constructive: build the monic splitting rings and their Artin bases, define the flag modules and the four coefficient maps, compute the rank-one intertwiner and its inverse by monic division, and verify each family of formal relations by the displayed polynomial identities.

1.1 Monic splitting and the vertex ring. Over the universal coefficient ring $S=k[c_1,\dots,c_N]$, adjoin roots of the monic framing polynomial one at a time and divide by the root: at step $s$ the residual polynomial is monic of degree $N-s+1$, so ordinary monic division preserves monicity. This produces the Artin basis $X_1^{a_1}\cdots X_N^{a_N}$, $0\le a_k\le N-k$, of the full root algebra; the pairing that reads the top coefficient has Gram matrix zero below the anti-diagonal and unit anti-diagonal in reversed order, hence is perfect over $S$, with no factorial division and no characteristic hypothesis. Block decomposition into the $r$ roots of $c_r$ and the $N-r$ roots of $b_{N-r}$ makes $L_m$ finite free over $C$ of rank $\binom Nr$, and $L_m=0$ for $r>N$ because then $p_m$ has degree below $r$. [F1, F2, F3, construct]

2.1 The vertex ring as a matrix quotient. Representing $\mathrm{NH}_r$ as the matrix algebra on its Artin module (step 1.1, [F2]) shows that the two-sided ideal generated by a monic $p(X_1)$ is the matrix ideal of the coefficients of the remainder of $p$ modulo $c_r$, and monic division makes these coefficients a unit triangular change from the consecutive relations; hence $\mathrm{NH}_r/(p(X_1))$ is the matrix algebra over the monic factor ring $L_m$ of the Statement. The same computation shows the $i$-flag $B_m$ is free of rank $N-r$ over $L_m$ and rank $r+1$ over $L_{m+i}$, giving the two root extensions of the model. [step 1.1, F2, F3, algebra]

3.1 The four coefficient maps and their triangles. For a monic $f$, the polynomial kernel $K_f(X,Y)=(f(X)-f(Y))/(X-Y)$ is defined before imposing $f(X)=f(Y)=0$ and satisfies $(X-Y)K_f=f(X)-f(Y)$ and $\tau_XK_f=1$; therefore $\tau_X(X^aK_f)=Y^a$ for every $a$, which identifies $K_f$ with the dual-power-basis Casimir of the two monic coefficient forms. The two Casimirs of $b_{N-r}$ and $c_{r+1}$ give the four displayed cups and caps; their contractions are the identities $\sum_av_a\tau(z^ab)=b$ and $\sum_a\tau(bv_a)z^a=b$ for dual Artin bases, and substituting them into the tensor composites proves both triangles of each of the two adjunctions. Degrees: $\tau_{\mathrm{old}}$ extracts $z^{N-r-1}$ and has degree $-2d_i(N-r-1)$; $\tau_{\mathrm{new}}$ extracts $z^r$ and has degree $-2d_ir$; the first maps have degree $0$ after the $B\{-2d_ir\}$ shift; the second cap has degree $-2d_i(N-r-1)+2d_ir=-2d_i(h_m-1)$, with inverse degree on its unit. Restoring the normalized $H_i$ at its input weight produces exactly the four formal degrees of [[def-minimal-parabolic-klr-diagram-proof-category]]. [step 2.1, algebra]

4.1 The rank-one intertwiner and its inverse. Splitting off one extra $i$-strand by the two-coset PBW decomposition [F3] gives the transfer term $\kappa_rb$ and the new-dot algebra as its complement; the rank-one intertwiner $g=(u-X)-(u-X)^2\kappa$ is verified to satisfy its quadratic and dot-commutation identities by expanding $\kappa X_{r+1}-X_r\kappa=1$ and $\kappa^2=0$. Multiplying these intertwiners along the extra strand and the other transfer by $p(X_1)$, then projecting to the polynomial complement, yields a coefficient map $A$ with $A(u^kS_r)=(-1)^ru^kp(u)$ where $S_r(u)=\prod_{a\le r}(u-X_a)^2$, and the same mixed relation gives $\phi_{k+1}(u)=u\phi_k+E(\psi_k)$; hence $A(u^k)=(-1)^r\operatorname{quo}_{S_r}(u^kp)$ by uniqueness of monic division, with no cyclotomic commutator theorem used as a supplier. If $h_m\ge0$ the quotients have distinct leading degrees $h_m+k$ and unit leading coefficients $(-1)^r$, so $\rho$ is the displayed (transfer, dot-power unit) map from $F_iE_i\{-2d_i\}$ plus the $h_m$ identity columns to $E_iF_i$, and its inverse subtracts the section and inverts the transfer. If $h_m\le0$ the map $A$ is surjective with kernel $\mathrm{span}\{1,u,\dots,u^{-h_m-1}\}$, and the connecting images have an anti-triangular dot/cap matrix with unit anti-diagonal, whose successive solution gives the negative-branch inverse. This verifies the rank-one matrix and both inverse equations of the formal definition. [step 2.1, step 3.1, F3, algebra]

5.1 Same-color crossing, curl and bubble identities. Equal crossings act by $\kappa=(s-1)/(X-Y)$, so $\kappa^2=0$, the braid relation holds and the two mixed dot equations follow from the rational divided-difference expansion; $K_f$ is symmetric, so its divided-difference correction vanishes and $(X-Y)K_f=f(X)-f(Y)$ gives the dot-mate equations. Contracting a crossing against either Casimir and using the rank-one block inverse of step 4.1 produces the cross-and-cap/curl equations: expanding $(f(X)-f(Y))/(X-Y)$ in the power bases and taking the top-coefficient rows gives the four signed sums over $a+b=-1$ and $a+b+c=-2$ with the stated orientation signs. The resulting oriented bubble Laurent series is $\Phi_i(u)=p_m(u)/c_r(u)^2$ of leading degree $h_m=N-2r$; its reciprocal is the opposite series with product $1$ coefficient by coefficient, forced by composing the two flag coefficient pairings, since each existing $i$ root contributes one factor from each side of the cap. Appending an $i$ root $z$ changes $\Phi_i$ to $\Phi_i/(u-z)^2$ and appending a spectator $j$ root $y$ changes it to $\Phi_iQ_{ij}(u,y)/t_{ij}$; expanding at infinity gives every finite bubble-slide coefficient equation. At a monic vacuum, $a_i(x)x^{\ell-1}=0$ gives $h_\ell+\sum_jc_{\lambda_i-j}h_{\ell-j}=0$ with $h_0=1$, $h_{<0}=0$, so $H(t)a_i^{\mathrm{rev}}(t)=1$. All coefficients use only addition, multiplication and monic formal inversion. [step 3.1, step 4.1, algebra]

6.1 Downward $Q$-relations and exact word grading. Give every flag the ordered shift $s_j(m)$ of the Statement. For $j<k$ the increasing word $(j,k)$ maps to the word $(k,j)$ by a quotient/switch of underlying degree $0$, with target-minus-source unit shift $-b_{jk}$; the reverse operator has underlying degree $-2b_{jk}$ and unit-shift $+b_{jk}$, so both have actual degree $-b_{jk}$, and same-color divided differences have degree $-2d_j$. Native operators are the negatives of the source operators, so their degrees and two-crossing composites are unchanged. The ordinary polynomial operators satisfy the idempotent, dot, far-commutation and quadratic $Q$-relations directly; expanding a three-strand composition gives zero difference for distinct outer colors and the divided difference of $Q$ for equal outer colors, and the global substitution $\kappa=-\tau$ changes all cubic signs to the native numerator. The quotient relations descend: on an $i,j$ pair $D_1$ has $bq=0$ and $D_0$ has $b=0$, and $Qb=t_{ij}bq$ makes multiplication by $Q$ well defined while the other crossing is the literal quotient. [step 2.1, step 3.1, step 5.1, algebra]

6.2 Mixed cups and caps with their constants. In $D[z]/p$ versus $D[z]/(pq)$ the coefficient form satisfies $\tau_{pq}(Qf)=t_{ij}\tau_p(f)$, because $Q=t_{ij}q$ and the leading coefficient of $Qf$ is $t_{ij}$ times that of $f$. For a full existing $i$-string use the ordered residue form $t_r^p(z)=(-1)^{r(N-r)}\operatorname{Res}\bigl(\Delta_r(X)X_1^{r-1}\cdots X_{r-1}\operatorname{Tr}(z)/\prod_ap(X_a)\bigr)$, in which no $1/r!$ occurs; expanding parabolic divided differences verifies this over the universal integral coefficient ring, and over its generic-root fraction field the sum over root orderings is the Vandermonde determinant whose two factors cancel the internal root-difference denominator, so the identity is an integral polynomial identity and specializes to every field. With $p'=pq$ and $U_r=\prod_aQ_{ij}(X_a,y)$, cancellation gives $t_r^{p'}(U_rz)=(-1)^{rA_{ij}}t_{ij}^rt_r^p(z)$, and perfectness of the model forms makes $U_r$ injective on the old quotient. Testing the relative cap against these forms gives $\pi_r\varepsilon_r^{p'}(Q(X_{r+1},y)\operatorname{lift}(z))=(-1)^{A_{ij}}t_{ij}\varepsilon_r^p(z)$ for every nil-Hecke coset element. Normalizing the second maps by the global weight sign $(-1)^{h+1}$ — legitimate because $N$ and $h$ have the same parity and the new $N$ changes by $A_{ij}$ — cancels that sign and gives the exact constant $t_{ij}$; dual-power-basis contraction gives the mixed-unit equation, and reversing colors gives $t_{ji}$ with the stated double-mate ratio. Native minus signs occur twice in these composites, so the scalars persist. [step 2.1, step 3.1, step 5.1, algebra]

7.1 Conclusion. Steps 3.1-6.2 verify every defining relation of [[def-minimal-parabolic-klr-diagram-proof-category]] on the explicit flag modules: the generators and their degrees, both adjunction triangles, the rank-one matrices in both branches with their inverses, the bubble series and slides, the cross-and-cap equations, the mixed isomorphism with its scalars, and the downward $Q$-relations. Monic extensions, their Casimirs, the finite rank-one inverses and the coefficient identities survive arbitrary monic specialization as ungraded maps, and the construction is choice-free. This proves only the formal MODEL relations; faithfulness and the cyclotomic word-corner transfer belong to separate suppliers. items.title: One-step simple restriction and induction, and the first-dot index
items.statement:
Let $k$ be any field and $R(Q)$ the graded KLR algebra for a real symmetrizable
Cartan datum and any homogeneous $Q$ satisfying the standing symmetry and
nonzero extremal-coefficient conditions. Graded simple modules are compared
up to internal shift. For a simple $S$ of root weight $\beta$ and
$r=\epsilon_i(S)>0$, its ordinary one-step last-$i$ restriction has a single
simple graded socle and a single simple graded head, each once and of the same
shift orbit, with $\epsilon_i=r-1$; its maximum-$\epsilon$ composition part has
coefficient a grading shift of $[r]_i$. The last-dot nilpotence index on that
restriction is exactly $r$. The first-end statements hold with
$\epsilon_i^L$ and the first dot. For every $n\ge1$,
$\operatorname{Ind}(S\boxtimes L(i^n))$ has a unique simple graded head
$f_i^nS$, occurring once in its whole composition series, with
$\epsilon_i=r+n$ (also when $r=0$); all other constituents have smaller
$\epsilon_i$. One-step simple socle and simple induction head are partial
inverses. A simple $S$ survives the first-strand cyclotomic quotient with
exponents $\lambda_i$ exactly when $\epsilon_i^L(S)\le\lambda_i$ for all $i$.
Right restriction preserves surviving simples, while projected right induction
has the same simple head when that generic head survives and is zero
otherwise. These are shift-orbit assertions and do not assert factorial socle
multiplicity.
items.strategy:
**Proof technique:** compute the nil-Hecke branching explicitly, then use adjunction, the maximal-tail recursion and the shuffle bound to pin the socle, head and dot index of one-step restriction, and read off the induction head and the cyclotomic survival criterion.

1.1 Nil-Hecke branching. Put $z=t_r$ and write $E_a$ for the elementary symmetric polynomials in $t_1,\dots,t_{r-1}$. The relations $e_a=E_a+zE_{a-1}=0$ give $E_a=(-z)^a$ for $1\le a\le r-1$, and the top relation gives $z^r=0$; hence $C_r=k[t_1,\dots,t_{r-1}]\otimes_{k[E_1,\dots,E_{r-1}]}k[z]/(z^r)$ with $E_a$ acting by $(-z)^a$. The polynomial representation of $\mathrm{NH}_{r-1}$ is free of rank $(r-1)!$ over its symmetric center and identifies $\mathrm{NH}_{r-1}$ with the matrix algebra over that center; after the specialization its image on $C_r$ is $\mathrm{Mat}_{(r-1)!}(k[z]/(z^r))$ with standard column $C_r$. Therefore the graded socle and head of $C_r$ are each one shifted copy of the nil-Hecke simple, the simple composition coefficient is a shift of $[r]_i$, multiplication by $z$ has nilpotence index exactly $r$, the socle is the column over $z^{r-1}k$ and the head the column modulo $z$. For $r=1$ this reads $C_1=k$, $z=0$. The same computation with the first variable distinguished gives first-end branching, and matrix units plus a monic Artin basis make it valid in every characteristic. More generally, induction of $L(i^r)\boxtimes L(i^n)$ is killed by the positive symmetric center: each total elementary symmetric function restricts to a sum of products of the positive elementary functions in the two blocks. Its dimension is $\binom{r+n}{r}r!n!=(r+n)!$ by the shuffle basis. The augmentation quotient of $\mathrm{NH}_{r+n}$ is the full matrix algebra with simple column dimension $(r+n)!$, so this induced module is one shifted copy of $L(i^{r+n})$. [F1, F4, algebra]

1.2 Simple socle of one-step restriction. Let $S$ have $r=\epsilon_i(S)>0$ and let $U\subseteq E_iS$ be a simple subobject with $t=\epsilon_i(U)$. The final dot $z$ commutes with $R(\beta-\alpha_i)$ and acts nilpotently on $E_iS$ (positive dot degree and finite graded support), preserving the socle and its ungraded isotypic components; on the isotypic component containing $U$ a nonzero power of $z$ has a nonzero kernel copy of the same simple type killed by $z$, and absolute simplicity and the finite graded semisimple decomposition let that copy be chosen homogeneously with the appropriate shift. Adjunction therefore produces a nonzero map $\operatorname{Ind}(U,L_1)\to S$, hence a surjection, and the shuffle bound [F4] gives $r\le t+1$ while the exact defining corners give $t\le r-1$; so $t=r-1$. [F1, F2, F4]

2.1 The maximal corner. Apply the maximal $(r-1)$-tail corner $p$ to $E_iS$, retaining $R(\beta-r\alpha_i)\otimes\mathrm{NH}_{r-1}$. By [F3], $\Delta_i^rS\cong N\boxtimes L(i^r)$ with $\epsilon_i(N)=0$, so $p(E_iS)=N\boxtimes\operatorname{Res}_{\mathrm{NH}_{r-1}}L(i^r)$; by step 1.1 and the absolute simplicity of $N$ this has a single simple socle. Every simple subobject $U$ of $E_iS$ has $t=r-1$ by step 1.2, so [F3] makes $pU$ a nonzero simple object; exactness of $p$ makes $p(\operatorname{soc}E_iS)$ semisimple and injects it into the one-simple socle of $p(E_iS)$. Hence $\operatorname{soc}E_iS$ is a single simple object, once, with $\epsilon_i=r-1$; moreover every nonzero submodule of $E_iS$ contains a simple graded submodule whose $p$-image is nonzero (detection). [step 1.2, F3]

3.1 Simple head, detection and the dot index. Finite graded duality $D$ is exact, takes simples to simples, fixes corner idempotents and commutes with restriction, so applying step 2.1 to $DS$ (same $\epsilon_i$) and dualising gives a single simple head of $E_iS$, once; the maximal corner of its head is the head of $N\boxtimes\operatorname{Res}L(i^r)$, while the maximal corner of its socle is that tensor's socle. By step 1.1 these are shifts of the same $N\boxtimes L(i^{r-1})$. The unique-head recursion of [F3] therefore identifies their simple shift orbits. On $p(E_iS)$, step 1.1 gives $z^r=0$ and $z^{r-1}\ne0$; the image of $z^r$ on all of $E_iS$ is a graded submodule with zero $p$-corner, so detection in step 2.1 forces it to be zero, while nonvanishing of $z^{r-1}$ in the corner forces it to be nonzero globally. Hence the last-dot nilpotence index on $E_iS$ is exactly $r$; repeating with the first variable gives first-dot index exactly $\epsilon_i^L(S)$. [step 2.1, F1, F2]

4.1 Nonreduced induction and its unique head. Put $M_n=\operatorname{Ind}(S\boxtimes L(i^n))$, $n\ge1$. Its maximum tail is at most $r+n$ by the shuffle bound; at tail $r+n$ the Mackey filtration retains exactly all $n$ added $i$-strands together with $r$ terminal $i$-strands of $S$, its surviving corner is $N\boxtimes\operatorname{Ind}_{\mathrm{NH}_r\otimes\mathrm{NH}_n}^{\mathrm{NH}_{r+n}}(L(i^r)\boxtimes L(i^n))$. The final computation of step 1.1 makes this $N\boxtimes L(i^{r+n})$ up to the fixed shift. Every simple quotient $T$ of $M_n$ has that maximum tail: adjunction gives a nonzero injection $S\boxtimes L(i^n)\hookrightarrow\Delta_i^nT$, and restricting the first factor to the maximal $r$-tail retains a nonzero corner of $T$'s maximal corner, so $\epsilon_i(T)\ge r+n$, and the shuffle bound gives equality. Hence the finite semisimple head of $M_n$ has only constituents detected by its simple maximal corner, so it is one simple constituent, once; the kernel of $M_n\to\operatorname{hd}M_n$ has zero maximal corner, so every other composition factor has smaller $\epsilon_i$ and the head occurs exactly once in the whole composition series. Write $f_iS:=\operatorname{hd}M_1$. [step 1.1, step 3.1, F3, F4]

5.1 Partial inverses, iterates and the cyclotomic criterion. Adjunction realises $S$ in $E_i(f_iS)$, so step 2.1 gives $\operatorname{soc}E_if_iS=S$ with shifts restored; conversely $S=\operatorname{soc}E_iT$ implies $T$ is a simple quotient of $\operatorname{Ind}(S,L_1)$, hence $T=f_iS$. Thus one-step socle and head are partial inverses, $f_i$ raises $\epsilon_i$ by one and $\operatorname{soc}E_i$ lowers it by one; iterating the one-strand argument gives $\operatorname{hd}\operatorname{Ind}(S\boxtimes L(i^n))=f_i^nS$. Let $J^\Lambda$ be generated by $x_1^{\lambda_i}$ on every word beginning with $i$; it annihilates a simple $S$ exactly when each first-$i$ corner has first-dot index at most $\lambda_i$, which by step 3.1 is $\epsilon_i^L(S)$, so $J^\Lambda S=0$ iff $\epsilon_i^L(S)\le\lambda_i$ for every $i$; if a generator is nonzero, simplicity forces $J^\Lambda S=S$. Right restriction preserves first strands, hence the cyclotomic subcategory; for induction, the generic unique head either survives, in which case the quotient induction has the same head, or dies, in which case the quotient induction is zero because every nonzero finite module has a simple quotient. The maximal-$\epsilon$ composition part is the same simple shift orbit as the head and socle, with coefficient a shift of $[r]_i$ by step 1.1. No choice and no self-dual representative is used. [step 2.1, step 3.1, step 4.1, F1, F2] ∎

items.title: PBW and bubble normal form in the minimal-parabolic diagram category
items.statement:
Fix a color $i$. In the formal graded minimal-parabolic proof category of
[[def-minimal-parabolic-klr-diagram-proof-category]], the reduced
perfect-matching diagrams, dot monomials on their open components, and
monomials in the independent far-left normalized $i$-bubble coefficients form
a basis of every morphism space. In particular, at all-downward boundaries of
weight difference $\beta$, the morphism space is the corresponding KLR PBW
corner tensored with the polynomial ring in one positive bubble family; the
opposite/fake family is its coefficientwise reciprocal. The graded polynomial
flag models of
[[lem-minimal-parabolic-polynomial-flag-model-realizes-the-graded-diagram-relations]],
with universal monic framing and arbitrarily large auxiliary framing at each
fixed physical source weight, are jointly faithful. The assertion is about this
formal proof category before cyclotomic quotient transfer.
items.strategy:
**Proof technique:** verify the bubble slides on the model, straighten an
arbitrary diagram by a finite lexicographic induction to a reduced matching
with dots and bubbles, and prove independence by a degree-separation argument
in the universal framed model.

1.1 Bubble slides on the model. For an $i$ root $x$ the normalized bubble series changes by $(1-xt)^{\pm2}$, and for a spectator $j$ root $y$ it changes by $q_{ij}^{\mathrm{rev}}(y,t)^{\pm1}$ with $q_{ij}^{\mathrm{rev}}=t^{-a_{ij}}Q_{ij}(t^{-1},y)/t_{ij}$ of constant coefficient $1$. These hold directly because the model series is $p^{\mathrm{rev}}/(c_r^{\mathrm{rev}})^2$, adjoining an $i$ root multiplies $c_r$ by $u-x$, and adjoining a spectator root multiplies $p$ by $Q_{ij}/t_{ij}$; every fixed inverse coefficient is a finite polynomial recursion. These are the specified formal relations, checked on the model and not derived from the faithfulness being proved. [F1, algebra]

2.1 Straightening to normal form. Move dots to fixed component positions using cyclicity and the KLR dot moves; an equal-color correction has one fewer crossing. Sort each $i$ cup/cap towards a boundary or the far-left closed-component position using the specified mate equations: a main term passes one of its finitely many crossing obstacles, and a correction term removes an unsorted open-component extremum or such an obstacle. Rank-one cross-and-cap sums are finite because open dot counts are nonnegative and negative-degree bubbles vanish, bounding the indices at each fixed total degree; adjacent opposed cup/cap pairs cancel by the triangles. Induct on the lexicographic pair (unsorted extrema, remaining crossing obstacles) and on crossing length for correction terms. Closed components have color $i$; cancel extra extrema, slide them left by the finite coefficient equations, and express the reverse family by bubble inversion. Coxeter deletion plus the KLR braid and quadratic straightening then reduce every open matching to the selected reduced diagram, all braid defects being shorter. This gives a finite spanning family of reduced matchings with dot monomials and far-left bubble monomials. [step 1.1, F1, F2]

3.1 All-downward boundaries. At an all-downward boundary every open arc joins bottom to top, so it is a colored permutation; the reduced matching together with its dots is exactly a KLR PBW monomial, and the morphism space is the PBW corner tensored with the polynomial ring in the positive bubble family, whose opposite family is the coefficientwise reciprocal by bubble inversion. For general boundaries the two triangles give invertible Hom correspondences bending the upward $i$-endpoints to the other boundary, and the straightening of step 2.1 has unit leading matching coefficients, so the same normal form transfers. [step 2.1, F1, F2]

4.1 Independence by degree separation. Fix the physical source weight $\mu$ and write $\mu_i=\langle h_i,\mu\rangle$; choose spectator background counts $m_j$ with $A_{\mathrm{spect}}=\sum_{j\ne i}(-a_{ij})m_j$ and for an increasing background $i$-count $r$ set $N=\mu_i+2r$, $\lambda_i=N-A_{\mathrm{spect}}$, so the physical weight $N-2r=\mu_i$ is fixed. Use the universal monic framing $a_i(u)=u^{\lambda_i}+z_1u^{\lambda_i-1}+\cdots+z_{\lambda_i}$ with independent $\deg z_a=2d_ia$, put $p=a_i\prod_{j\ne i}Q_{ij}/t_{ij}$ and $c_r=\prod_a(u-x_a)$; the normalized series $\mathcal B(t)=p^{\mathrm{rev}}/(c_r^{\mathrm{rev}})^2=a_i^{\mathrm{rev}}U(t)$ with $U_0=1$ has coefficients $\mathcal B_a=z_a+\sum_{1\le\ell<a}z_\ell U_{a-\ell}+U_a$, unit triangular in the framing variables, with reciprocal coefficients $-z_a$ plus lower framing indices. Hence the first $D$ bubble coefficients are independent whenever $\lambda_i\ge D$, in every characteristic and at every physical weight; no unit old-root coefficient is claimed, since $\mathcal B_1=p_1+2e_1$ can lose its root term in characteristic two. A nonzero finite PBW/bubble combination remains nonzero after this triangular substitution over the independent polynomial coefficient domain; the generic KLR polynomial representation has a distinct nonzero leading permutation for each selected crossing word, so a polynomial test vector with nonzero output exists after clearing a finite denominator. Let $D$ bound the bubble indices and $B$ the actual internal degrees of that vector and its output, both finite in the untruncated polynomial ring, and let $L$ bound the number of added $i$-flags tested. Every monic flag relation and factor-ring coefficient relation after those flags has degree at least $2d_i(\mu_i+r-L+1)$, spectator appends only increase $N$, all variables are nonnegatively graded and all dot degrees are positive; choosing $r\ge0$ and $\lambda_i\ge D$ with $2d_i(\mu_i+r-L+1)>B$ (possible at fixed $\mu$) separates all model relations from degree $\le B$, so the nonzero PBW output survives in that flag model. [step 3.1, F1]

5.1 Conclusion. The family of step 2.1 spans every morphism space by a finite straightening, and step 4.1 shows that no nonzero combination of its reduced matchings, dot monomials and independent bubble monomials vanishes in some graded flag model, so the family is a basis and the stated models are jointly faithful. The model's ordered word shifts with $i$ last make every crossing homogeneous of degree $-b_{jk}$, and the formal upward generator is the normalized $H_i$, so the witness is a witness in the specified graded model; the assertion concerns the formal proof category before any cyclotomic quotient transfer. [step 2.1, step 3.1, step 4.1] ∎

items.title: Cyclotomic induction is projective on the right
items.statement:
Let $R^\Lambda$ be the cyclotomic KLR algebra of
[[def-cyclotomic-klr-quotient-at-a-dominant-weight]], and let
$E^\Lambda_i,F^\Lambda_i$ be the functors of
[[def-cyclotomic-klr-induction-and-restriction-functors]]. For every $i\in I$
and $\beta\in Q_+$:

(a) the bimodule $R^\Lambda(\beta+\alpha_i)e(\beta,i)$ is a projective right
$R^\Lambda(\beta)$-module, and $e(\beta,i)R^\Lambda(\beta+\alpha_i)$ is a
projective left $R^\Lambda(\beta)$-module;

(b) consequently $E^\Lambda_i$ and $F^\Lambda_i$ are exact and send finitely
generated graded projectives to finitely generated graded projectives;
moreover $F^\Lambda_i$ preserves all projectives and $E^\Lambda_i$ preserves
finitely generated ones;

(c) there is a functorial exact sequence in
$\mathrm{Mod}(R(\beta+\alpha_i))$
$$0\longrightarrow q^{(\alpha_i\mid 2\Lambda-\beta)}\bar F_iM\longrightarrow F_iM\longrightarrow F^\Lambda_iM\longrightarrow 0,\qquad M\in\mathrm{Mod}(R^\Lambda(\beta)),$$
where $F_i$ is the right-append and $\bar F_i$ the left-append generic
induction of
[[lem-generic-klr-induction-and-restriction-mixed-relations]], regarded on
$R^\Lambda$-modules through the quotient, and the exponent is the Cartan
pairing $(\alpha_i\mid 2\Lambda-\beta)=2(\alpha_i\mid\Lambda)
-(\alpha_i\mid\beta)$
([[def-quantum-integers-factorials-and-divided-powers-at-q-i]] records the
normalization of the powers of $q$).
items.strategy:
**Proof technique:** compare the cyclotomic towers over the generic ones with an explicit monic comparison map, then use the monic-annihilator projective splitting to deduce projectivity, exactness and the exact sequence with its shift.

If $A=0$, the comparison modules and functor values are zero, so all assertions are vacuous; polynomial degrees below are used only for $A

1.1 Comparison modules and their projectivity. Put $n=| eta|$ and let $R_1( eta)=\xi_nR( eta)$ act on positions $2,\ldots,n+1$. For $n>0$ set $J_0=Sa(x_1)R( eta)e_R$ and $J_1=Sa(x_2)R_1( eta)e_L$; for $n=0$ set $J_0=J_1=0$, since the old block has no cyclotomic relation. Put $K_0=Se_R/J_0$, $K_1=Se_L/J_1$. The right action of $A[t]$ on $K_0$ uses the first $n$ strands and $t=x_{n+1}$; on $K_1$ it uses $\xi_n$ and $t=x_1$. The labelled PBW cosets make $Se_R$ and $Se_L$ finite projective over the corresponding separated-block algebras $R( eta)[t]$: each homogeneous coset summand is a shifted principal word-idempotent module. Tensoring these summands with $A[t]$ gives precisely $K_0,K_1$, so both are finite projective over $A[t]$. At $n=0$ both are $k[t]$. [F1, F2, algebra]

1.2 Monic annihilators and projectivity, locally. Let $0	o P_1\xrightarrow{j}P_0	o M	o0$ be an exact sequence of right $A[t]$-modules with finite projective $P_0,P_1$, and suppose a central monic $f$ annihilates $M$. Multiplication by $f$ is injective on a free $A[t]$-module by its unit leading coefficient, hence on its projective summands. On a finite free module monic division gives an $A$-linear operator $p_{\mathrm{free}}$ taking a polynomial to its quotient by $f$, with $p_{\mathrm{free}}(xf)=x$. Equivalently, $P_r/fP_r$ is a summand of $(A[t]/fA[t])^N\cong A^{mN}$ and is $A$-projective, which is the monic-quotient reason for the splitting. Each mixed-relation correction omits one transfer crossing and has the form, up to its color projector and sign, $(\kappa_{a+1}\cdots\kappa_n)a(x_1)\kappa_1\cdots\kappa_{a-1}$, hence belongs to $J_0$. Moving $\kappa_{a+1}$ to $\kappa_a$ introduces only the braid correction $a(x_1)\kappa_1\cdots\kappa_{a-1}D_a\kappa_{a+2}\cdots\kappa_n$, with $D_a$ a dot polynomial; the far crossings can be moved left and the last-dot powers commute with the shorter word, again putting it in $J_0$. Independence of the permutation operators then forces every coefficient to vanish. Consequently right multiplication by $g_n\cdots g_1$ intertwines old dots/crossings with their shifted copies and $x_{n+1}$ with $x_1$. It descends to $Q:K_0	o K_1$: the first-position cosets write $J_0$ as the sum of the terms $Sa(x_1)\kappa_1\cdots\kappa_r e_R$, $r<n$, and the intertwining identities send each such term to $Sg_n\cdots g_1a(x_2)\kappa_2\cdots\kappa_{r+1}e_L\subseteq J_1$.
