items.title: The cyclotomic cap-off quotient has no extra downward relations
items.statement:
Let $\Lambda$ be dominant, $\lambda_j=\langle h_j,\Lambda\rangle$, and let
$\mathcal P_i$ be [[def-minimal-parabolic-klr-diagram-proof-category]], with
its homogeneous polynomial realization and PBW/bubble normal form. Fix monic
$a_j(u)=u^{\lambda_j}+\sum_{r<\lambda_j}c_{j,r}u^r$; for the standard graded
cyclotomic quotient take $a_j(u)=u^{\lambda_j}$ as in
[[def-cyclotomic-klr-quotient-at-a-dominant-weight]]. More generally first take
universal graded coefficients of degree $2d_j(\lambda_j-r)$; arbitrary monic
specializations over the field are interpreted as ungraded.

In the representable category $\mathcal P_i(\Lambda)$, let $J$ be the ideal
generated by $1_{H_iv_\Lambda}$ and $a_j(x)1_{G_jv_\Lambda}$ for every $j$,
closed under arbitrary vertical pre/postcomposition and horizontal whiskering
by the allowed $1$-morphisms. For downward words $\mu,\nu$ of the same weight
$\beta$, include their ordinary KLR corner by the PBW/bubble normal form. Then
$$J\cap e(\nu)R(\beta)e(\mu)=e(\nu)I_a(\beta)e(\mu),\qquad I_a(\beta)=\sum_jR(\beta)a_j(x_1)e(j,\beta-\alpha_j)R(\beta).$$
The vacuum bubble specialization is forced by these generators:
$A_\Lambda(t)=1+c_{i,\lambda_i-1}t+\cdots+c_{i,0}t^{\lambda_i}$ and
$\mathsf H_\Lambda=A_\Lambda^{-1}$. Consequently the map from the ordinary
monic cyclotomic corner to the downward-word Hom corner of
$\mathcal P_i(\Lambda)/J$ is an isomorphism, with composition corresponding to
multiplication. This holds over every degree-zero field for the entire
admissible homogeneous $Q$ family, without finite-type or characteristic-zero
restrictions. Inhomogeneous monic specializations assert the ungraded corner
equality, not a graded quantum-action conclusion.
items.strategy:
**Proof technique:** force the vacuum bubble coefficients by the rank-one
recurrence, use the normal form to see that specializing them introduces no
downward relation, then identify the quotient corner with the ordinary monic
cyclotomic corner generator by generator.

1.1 Vacuum coefficients are forced. Use the normalized trace cups and caps of [F1] and let $h_\ell$ be the bubble closed with $\lambda_i-1+\ell$ dots, with negative-dot symbols extended by the formal inversion of [F1]. The rank-one identities give $h_\ell=0$ for $\ell<0$ and $h_0=1$. Closing $a_i(x)x^{\ell-1}=0$ for $\ell\ge1$ is lawful in the defining ideal because the exponent $\ell-1$ is nonnegative even when some resulting bubble indices are negative, and gives $h_\ell+c_{i,\lambda_i-1}h_{\ell-1}+\cdots+c_{i,0}h_{\ell-\lambda_i}=0$. Hence $H(t)=\sum_{\ell\ge0}h_\ell t^\ell$ is the inverse of $a_i^{\mathrm{rev}}(t)=1+c_{i,\lambda_i-1}t+\cdots+c_{i,0}t^{\lambda_i}$, and bubble inversion gives $A(t)=H(t)^{-1}=a_i^{\mathrm{rev}}(t)$; each coefficient uses only a finite recurrence. An actual vacancy loop with $r\ge0$ dots has $A$-index $\lambda_i+1+r$ and vanishes because $A$ has degree at most $\lambda_i$, while the $A$-coefficients of index $1,\dots,\lambda_i$ are fake bubbles of negative dot count, prescribed rather than zero; for $a_i=u(u-1)$ one gets $A=1-t$, $H=(1-t)^{-1}$, so setting all positive bubbles to zero would wrongly change the deformation. If $\lambda_i=0$ then $a_i=1$ kills $F_iv$ and $A=H=1$. [F1, algebra]

2.1 Every bubble coefficient is brought to the vacuum. After bending, a coefficient may be a bubble at $\Lambda+\alpha_i$ immediately to the left of an added first $i$-strand with dot $z$; the rank-one bubble-slide equation in coefficient normalization is $A_{\Lambda+\alpha_i}(t)=(1-zt)^2A_\Lambda(t)$ and $H_{\Lambda+\alpha_i}(t)=(1-zt)^{-2}H_\Lambda(t)$. These are normalized power series with constant coefficient $1$, and for each fixed coefficient the equation is finite polynomial in $z$ and the vacuum coefficients; negative exponents of $(1-zt)$ denote formal coefficient recursion. The algebraic verification is the model computation: with total monic polynomial $p$ and existing-root factor $c_r$ the normalized series is $p^{\mathrm{rev}}/(c_r^{\mathrm{rev}})^2$, and adding the distinguished root $z$ replaces $c_r^{\mathrm{rev}}$ by $c_r^{\mathrm{rev}}(1-zt)$ and leaves $p^{\mathrm{rev}}$ unchanged; passing to the reciprocals gives the displayed pair. [step 1.1, F1, algebra]

3.1 Specializing the vacuum coefficients adds no downward relation. Let $S$ be the vacuum bubble coefficient specialization of step 1.1. By the recurrence $S$ is contained in $J$. By the tensor-product normal form [F2], specializing these central vacuum coefficients alone gives the all-downward corner $R(\beta)$ with no relation imposed in its ordinary polynomial and crossing part; this uses the normal form, not a flatness assertion. One may therefore compute in $\mathcal P_i/S$ first and then include the $E_i$ and first-strand generators, with every bubble coefficient brought to the vacuum by step 2.1. [step 2.1, F2]

4.1 The corner identification. Let $x\in J\cap e(\nu)R(\beta)e(\mu)$. Expanding $x$ in the normal form of [F2] and using steps 2.1-3.1 to substitute every bubble coefficient by its vacuum value, $x$ is a combination of the generators $1_{H_iv_\Lambda}$ and $a_j(x)1_{G_jv_\Lambda}$ whiskered and composed with downward diagrams; the whiskering of $1_{H_iv_\Lambda}$ into a downward word contributes only the first-strand $a$-terms through the triangles, while the $a_j(x)$-generators contribute exactly the ordinary two-sided ideal $I_a(\beta)=\sum_jR(\beta)a_j(x_1)e(j,\beta-\alpha_j)R(\beta)$. Conversely every element of $e(\nu)I_a(\beta)e(\mu)$ lies in $J$ by construction. Hence the intersection is exactly $e(\nu)I_a(\beta)e(\mu)$, and the same expansion shows the map from the ordinary monic cyclotomic corner $e(\nu)R(\beta)e(\mu)/e(\nu)I_a(\beta)e(\mu)$ to the corresponding Hom corner of $\mathcal P_i(\Lambda)/J$ is an isomorphism compatible with composition. [step 3.1, F2, F3]

5.1 Conclusion. Steps 1.1-4.1 prove the forced vacuum specialization, the corner equality and the isomorphism, over every degree-zero field and for the whole admissible homogeneous $Q$ family; in the inhomogeneous monic case the same argument is performed without grading and asserts only the ungraded corner equality, and no finite-type, characteristic-zero, faithfulness or generic Frobenius input is used. [step 4.1] ∎

items.title: The two-colour jump formula and strict elementary embeddings
items.statement:
Let $k$ be any field and $R(Q)$ the graded KLR algebra for a real symmetrizable
Cartan datum and any homogeneous $Q$ satisfying the standing symmetry and
nonzero extremal-coefficient conditions. Graded simple modules are compared up
to internal shift. Set $c_i(S)=\epsilon_i^L(S)$ and
$J_i(S)=\max\{n\ge0:c_i(f_i^nS)=c_i(S)\}$. This maximum is finite and
$J_i(S)=\epsilon_i(S)+c_i(S)-\langle h_i,\beta\rangle$ for
$S$ of root weight $\beta\in Q_+$. For $i\ne j$ one has $c_i(f_jS)=c_i(S)$; for
$j=i$ it stays constant or increases by $1$, and increase is equivalent to
$f_iS=f_i^LS$ and to simplicity of $\operatorname{Ind}(S,L(i))$. Once it
increases, it increases at every later right-$i$ step. Put
$\operatorname{wt}(S)=-\beta$ and $\phi_i=\epsilon_i+\langle h_i,
\operatorname{wt}\rangle$. The maps
$\Psi_i(S)=(e_i^L)^{c_i(S)}S\otimes b_i(-c_i(S))$ are strict injective
elementary-crystal maps, and every nonvacuum simple has positive extraction at
some $i$. The simple graph is lowering-generated with every generic $f_i$
nonzero. In any first-strand cyclotomic quotient containing $S$ the actual
surviving lowering length is
$\lambda_i+\epsilon_i(S)-\langle h_i,\beta\rangle$. All containing-weight
arguments take place in the auxiliary primitive-coroot finite-support datum,
leaving $R,A,D,Q$ unchanged, so no positive-dominant-label assumption on the
original $P$ is added. Linear divided restriction/$G_0$ operators satisfy the
quantum Serre relation; the simple-socle crystal operators are not asserted to
satisfy a linear Serre identity.
items.strategy:
**Proof technique:** prove the two-colour structure directly with nil-Hecke columns, obtain a finite jump from a containing cyclotomic quotient, calculate its initial value by containing-weight annihilation and induction from the vacuum, and verify every elementary tensor branch.

1.1 Work on the finite support supplied by [F2], prescribing the cyclotomic labels independently there. Write $L_r=L(i^r)$, $c_i=\epsilon_i^L$, and write $\operatorname{Ind}(A,B)$ for induction of the external tensor product; all module identifications below are on shift orbits. Two consequences of exact induction will be used. A surjection $\operatorname{Ind}(A,H)\to T$ with $T$ simple induces a surjection $\operatorname{Ind}(A,U)\to T$ for some simple composition factor $U$ of $H$: take the first nonzero image in an induced composition series. If $\epsilon_i(A)=0$, a nonzero map $\operatorname{Ind}(A,U)\to T$ with $A,U,T$ simple forces $\epsilon_i(T)=\epsilon_i(U)$, since the shuffle bound gives the upper bound and adjunction injects $A\boxtimes U$ into the defining restriction, giving the lower bound. More particularly, a surjection $\operatorname{Ind}(A,B,L_h)\to T$ with $\epsilon_i(A)=0$ factors through $\operatorname{Ind}(A,f_i^hB)\to T$: its tail is $\epsilon_i(B)+h$, whereas every constituent of the kernel of $\operatorname{Ind}(B,L_h)\to f_i^hB$ has smaller tail by [F1], so an induced composition series of that kernel has zero image in $T$. [F1, F2, algebra]

1.2 Here is the rank-two structure needed below, including its parameter calculation. Fix $j\ne i$, put $a=-a_{ij}$ and $t=[u^a]Q_{ij}(u,v)\in k^\times$. For $p+q\le a$, define $L(i^pji^q)$ to have only the word $i^pji^q$ in its support, with column $L_p\boxtimes L(j)\boxtimes L_q$, the $j$-dot zero and both crossings adjacent to $j$ zero. All relations hold: $Q_{ij}(u,0)=tu^a$, which kills either neighbouring column, and the native $i,j,i$ braid correction is $-t\sum_{r=0}^{a-1}x^rz^{a-1-r}$. Each monomial kills the column since $r\ge p$ or $a-1-r\ge q$ when $p+q\le a$. The other mixed and braid equations have zero terms or are internal nil-Hecke equations. This module is simple by the matrix-column calculation in [F1], with right tail $q$, first tail $p$ and ungraded character $p!q!i^pji^q$. These are all simples of weight $ci+j$ when $c\le a$: induct on $c$; a simple with positive right tail is the unique $f_i$-image of its predecessor, whose tail identifies the constructed column; a simple of right tail zero is supported only on $i^cj$, and the same column argument gives $L(i^cj)$. For $c>a$ no simple can have right tail zero: such a module would again be the column $L_c\boxtimes L(j)$ supported only on $i^cj$, but the last mixed crossing has square $t x_c^a$, nonzero on $L_c$ since its dot index is $c$. This contradicts its zero crossing. [F1, F3, algebra, construct]

2.1 Adjunction and the shuffle bound give $c_i(M)\le c_i(f_jM)\le c_i(M)+\delta_{ij}$; first-end symmetry gives $\epsilon_j(f_i^LM)=\epsilon_j(M)$ for $j\ne i$. If $c_i(f_iM)=c_i(M)+1$, then $f_iM=f_i^LM$: the two orders of induction have the same character at $q=1$ and hence the same ungraded composition multiplicities, while the first order's factor with maximum first tail is uniquely $f_i^LM$, once. The character implication here follows from the triangular divided-word/projective pairing in [F1]: divided-word corner dimensions are obtained from ordinary word-corner dimensions by dividing the corresponding nil-Hecke block factorials at $q=1$, and their triangular matrix with diagonal $1$ remains invertible there. Conversely, equality of the two simple heads forces the increase. The coinduction formula in [F1], together with maximal-tail restriction, gives $\operatorname{soc}\operatorname{Ind}(M,L_h)=(f_i^L)^hM$ and $\operatorname{soc}\operatorname{Ind}(L_h,M)=f_i^hM$: coinduction has only one simple socle, since every simple subobject has the maximum tail by adjunction and its simple maximum corner detects it. Thus $f_iM=f_i^LM$ forces $\operatorname{Ind}(M,L_1)$ simple: its head and socle agree and this factor occurs once; in a nonsimple module the socle would lie in the radical and supply a second occurrence. Conversely simplicity forces its socle and head to agree. Commuting $M$ successively past the $h$ single-colour factors, and using $\operatorname{Ind}(L_r,L_s)=L_{r+s}$, gives $\operatorname{Ind}(M,L_h)=\operatorname{Ind}(L_h,M)$; its simple head equals its simple socle and occurs once, so it too is simple. Hence one increase forces increases at all later steps. [step 1.1, F1, F3, algebra]

3.1 Put $D_n=L(i^{a-n}ji^n)$ for $0\le n\le a$. The module $\operatorname{Ind}(D_n,L_1)$ has only two word corners, $i^{a-n}ji^{n+1}$ and $i^{a-n+1}ji^n$, each a simple product of nil-Hecke columns by [F1]. Its simple head has the first corner nonzero. The linear divided restriction Serre relation forces the second corner nonzero too: when applied to that head at weight $(a+1)i+j$, all terms $E_i^{(a+1-s)}E_jE_i^{(s)}$ vanish except $s=n,n+1$, and the $s=n+1$ term is nonzero. The relation is available on finite modules by applying homogeneous Hom to the split projective Serre identity; exact projective Hom and the unscaled pairing in [F1] identify these Hom spaces with the divided corners. Thus the head fills both simple corners and induction is simple, so $f_iD_n=f_i^LD_n$. Step 2.1 proves $\operatorname{Ind}(D_n,L_h)=\operatorname{Ind}(L_h,D_n)$ simple for every $h$. For $c\ge a$, induction on $c$ now classifies all simples of weight $ci+j$ as $\operatorname{Ind}(D_n,L_{c-a})$, $0\le n\le a$, with right tail $n+c-a$: step 1.2 excludes right tail zero for $c>a$, and the one-step partial inverse identifies every positive-tail simple from the preceding weight. For $a=0$, $Q_{ij}$ is a nonzero constant, the mixed crossing is invertible, and $\operatorname{Ind}(L(j),L_h)=\operatorname{Ind}(L_h,L(j))$ is the unique simple, giving the same classification. No characteristic, splitting-field or special binomial-parameter assumption was used. [step 2.1, step 1.2, F1, F5, algebra]

3.2 Define $v_i^\lambda(M)$ as the number of surviving right-$i$ lowering steps in a quotient with labels $\lambda$ containing $M$. It is finite by [F4]. Choose such labels with $\lambda_l\ge c_l(M)$, possible by [F2] and [F1]. If $c_i(f_i^nM)$ never increased, step 2.1 would keep every first tail within those labels for every $n$, contrary to [F4]. Hence $J_i(M)$ is finite; more explicitly, the bound $B_i(\beta,\lambda)$ of [F4] with $R^\lambda(\beta+B_i\alpha_i)=0$ gives $J_i(M)<B_i(\beta,\lambda)$. Step 2.1 gives, for all $h\ge0$, $c_i(f_i^hM)=c_i(M)+\max(0,h-J_i(M))$, and the other first tails are unchanged. The survival criterion in [F1] therefore gives $ v_i^\lambda(M)=J_i(M)+\lambda_i-c_i(M)$. In particular differences $v_i^\lambda(X)-v_i^\lambda(Y)$ for two surviving simples are independent of the containing labels, and $J_i(f_iM)=\max(0,J_i(M)-1)$. This proves finiteness and the recurrence without using the numerical jump formula. [step 2.1, F1, F2, F4, algebra]

3.3 For extraction put $c=c_i(M)$ and $U=(e_i^L)^cM$, so $M=(f_i^L)^cU$ and $c_i(U)=0$. If $c_i(f_jM)=c$, then $(e_i^L)^cf_jM=f_jU$. Indeed induce $L_c,U,L(j)$ onto $f_jM$ and apply maximal first-$i$ restriction, then its simple quotient. In the Mackey filtration the $U$-contribution of first $i$'s is zero; for $j\ne i$ the only surviving factors after forgetting the first column are shifts of $\operatorname{Ind}(U,L(j))$. Thus the target is its unique simple head. For $j=i$ there can also be shifts of $\operatorname{Ind}(L(i),U)$, but these have no nonzero map to the extracted target of first tail zero, by adjunction; the same unique-head conclusion follows. If $c_i(f_iM)=c+1$, step 2.1 instead gives $e_i^Lf_iM=M$ and therefore extraction yields $U$. For $j\ne i$, $\epsilon_j(U)=\epsilon_j(M)$ because first-$i$ lowering preserves the right $j$-tail (step 2.1). The preceding lowering compatibility and partial inverses then give extraction compatibility with $e_j$ whenever $e_jM\ne0$; when $e_jM=0$, the equality of tails makes $e_jU=0$ too. [step 1.1, step 2.1, F1, algebra]

4.1 We record the two containing-weight annihilation tests, with their proofs. If $A$ survives and $k=v_i^\lambda(A)$, then the quotient of $\operatorname{Ind}(A,L_{k+1})$ is zero: its only simple head is the killed $f_i^{k+1}A$, while any nonzero finite quotient has a simple head. Appending any further block preserves zero, since a cyclotomic relation on an initial block is also a relation on the larger initial block. Consequently $\operatorname{Ind}(A,B)$ has zero quotient if $c_i(B)>k$, by the surjection $\operatorname{Ind}(L_{c_i(B)},(e_i^L)^{c_i(B)}B)\to B$. Conversely suppose $\epsilon_i(A)=\epsilon_j(A)=0$, $B$ has weight $ci+dj$, and $\operatorname{Ind}(A,B)\to T$ is surjective and simple. If $b=c_i(B)\le k$, write $C=(e_i^L)^bB$ and induce $A,L_b,C$. Its map to $T$ factors through $f_i^bA,C$: all other constituents $U$ of $\operatorname{Ind}(A,L_b)$ have $\epsilon_i(U)<b$. The defining corner of $T$ with an initial block of weight $\operatorname{wt}_{\rm root}(A)$ followed by a suffix of colours $i,j$ and beginning with $i^b$ is nonzero by adjunction. Every word in any such $U$ has a non-$i,j$ letter after the original $A$-block length: otherwise its last $A$-letter, necessarily different from $i,j$, would already lie in that initial block and all $b$ added $i$'s would be a tail, contradicting $\epsilon_i(U)<b$. Shuffling with $C$ preserves that non-$i,j$ letter in the suffix, so this corner vanishes on $\operatorname{Ind}(U,C)$. Thus no such factor maps onto $T$, proving the factorisation. The shuffle bound gives $c_i(T)\le c_i(f_i^bA)+c_i(C)\le\lambda_i$. Taking $\lambda_j$ larger than the total root-height of the finitely many modules being considered makes the $j$ inequality automatic; other first tails of $T$ are at most those of $A$. Hence this converse guarantees survival. In these comparisons we may enlarge every label except $\lambda_i$ to cover the fixed non-$i$ content of all the $i$-strings, so no assertion of a converse for a small $\lambda_j$ is needed. [step 1.1, step 3.2, F1, F2, algebra]

4.2 First calculate the containing-length change in rank two. Any simple $N$ of weight $ci+dj$ with $\epsilon_i(N)=0$ is a quotient of $\operatorname{Ind}(L(i^{b_1}j),\ldots,L(i^{b_r}j))$ with $0\le b_s\le a$: strip one right $j$, then its maximal $i$-tail, and repeat. A positive-height $N$ has a right $j$ since its right $i$ is zero; the factors of $\operatorname{Ind}(L_b,L(j))$ are classified by step 3.1, so tail zero forces $b\le a$ and the unique factor $L(i^bj)$. This justifies each factor selection by step 1.1 and decreases height, so the process terminates. For arbitrary $M$, put $m=\epsilon_i(M)$ and strip that tail to obtain such an $N$. The simple $f_jM$ is a quotient induced from $N$ and a factor $U$ of $\operatorname{Ind}(L_m,L(j))$. Step 1.1 determines its tail $\gamma=\epsilon_i(U)$; by step 3.1 it equals $m-a+n$ for some $0\le n\le a$ and $ f_i^aU=\operatorname{Ind}(D_n,L_m)$. This holds also for $m<a$, where $U=L(i^{a-n}ji^{m-a+n})$ and $m-a+n\ge0$. [step 1.1, step 1.2, step 3.1, algebra]

5.1 For any simple $B$, every simple quotient of $\operatorname{Ind}(B,D_n)$ has right tail $\epsilon_i(B)+n$: strip the right tail $L_{\epsilon_i(B)}$ of $B$, commute it past $D_n$ by step 3.1, and split $D_n$ as the head of $L(i^{a-n}j),L_n$. The resulting surjection with terminal block $L_{\epsilon_i(B)+n}$ gives the lower bound by adjunction; the shuffle bound gives the upper bound. This also holds for a string of $D_n$ factors by iteration. Let $d_s=a-b_s$ and $D=\sum_s d_s$. For $m+h\ge D$, the surjection from the factors in step 4.2 to $f_i^hM$ can be rewritten as a surjection $\operatorname{Ind}(D_{d_1},\ldots,D_{d_r},L_{m+h-D})\to f_i^hM$. To verify it, start at the rightmost $L(i^{b_r}j)$: the unique constituent of $\operatorname{Ind}(L(i^{b_r}j),L_{m+h})$ with tail $m+h$ is $\operatorname{Ind}(D_{d_r},L_{m+h-d_r})$ by step 3.1. Every other constituent has smaller tail and cannot map to the target through the preceding tail-zero factors by step 1.1. Commute this $D_{d_r}$ past the remaining pure-colour block using step 3.1 and repeat with $r-1,\ldots,1$. Each suffix of the $d_s$ has sum at most $D$, so all consumed block lengths are nonnegative. If a simple $Q$ is a quotient of $\operatorname{Ind}(D_{n_1},\ldots,D_{n_r},L_g)$, its right and first tails are exactly $g+\sum_s n_s$ and $g+\sum_s(a-n_s)$. Indeed commute $L_g$ past each $D_{n_s}$, split $D_{n_s}$ as the head of $L(i^{a-n_s}j),L_{n_s}$, and move its $L_{n_s}$ to the right; adjunction gives the lower right-tail bound, the shuffle bound the matching upper bound. Repeat with the first-end split to obtain the first-tail bound. Therefore, with $C=m-ar+2\sum_s b_s$, we have $c_i(f_i^hM)=h+C$ for $h$ sufficiently large. For $f_i^hf_jM$ first absorb $a$ pure strands into $U$ using step 4.2 and the factorisation of step 1.1, and perform the same replacements on the preceding factors. For $h\ge a+D$ this gives a quotient of $\operatorname{Ind}(D_{d_1},\ldots,D_{d_r},D_n,L_{m+h-a-D})$, whose first tail is $h+C-n$. Choose $h$ still larger so both these tails are nonnegative and take the containing $i$ label to be $\omega_i=h+C$, with other labels large. The next first tail of $M$ is $\omega_i+1$, whereas $f_jM$ survives exactly $h+n$ steps. Thus $v_i^\omega(f_jM)-v_i^\omega(M)=n$; label independence in step 3.2 gives for every quotient containing both $ v_i^\lambda(f_jM)-v_i^\lambda(M)=n=\epsilon_i(f_jM)-\epsilon_i(M)+a$. This is the rank-two containing-length calculation, with an actual finite saturation threshold. [step 1.1, step 3.1, step 3.2, step 4.2, F2, algebra]

6.1 Reduce an arbitrary $M$ and $f_jM$ to that calculation. First strip the right $i$-tail of $M$, then alternately strip maximal right $j$- and $i$-tails until the remaining simple $A$ has $\epsilon_i(A)=\epsilon_j(A)=0$; each nonzero stripping decreases root-height. Group the removed blocks into a simple rank-two factor $B_0$ with a surjection $\operatorname{Ind}(A,B_0)\to e_i^{\epsilon_i(M)}M$, by step 1.1. Append the removed $i$-tail and apply the factorisation of step 1.1 to get $\operatorname{Ind}(A,B)\to M$ with $B=f_i^{\epsilon_i(M)}B_0$. For both $l=i,j$, the corner lower bound and shuffle upper bound give $\epsilon_l(B)=\epsilon_l(M)$. Appending $j$ and applying step 1.1 with colour $j$ gives $\operatorname{Ind}(A,f_jB)\to f_jM$, also with $\epsilon_i(f_jB)=\epsilon_i(f_jM)$. The same factorisation gives $\operatorname{Ind}(A,f_i^hB)\to f_i^hM$ and $\operatorname{Ind}(A,f_i^{h'}f_jB)\to f_i^{h'}f_jM$ for all $h,h'$. Choose containing labels $\omega$ for these initial modules with all non-$i$ labels large, and set $h=v_i^\omega(M)$, $h'=v_i^\omega(f_jM)$ and $k=v_i^\omega(A)$. The two annihilation tests in step 4.1 imply $c_i(f_i^hB)\le k<c_i(f_i^{h+1}B)$ and $c_i(f_i^{h'}f_jB)\le k<c_i(f_i^{h'+1}f_jB)$. Step 2.1 makes the inequalities equalities at the surviving endpoints and gives zero jump there. Step 3.2, applied to $B$ and $f_jB$, now gives $v_i^\omega(B)=h+\omega_i-k$ and $v_i^\omega(f_jB)=h'+\omega_i-k$. Their difference equals $h'-h$; step 5.1 evaluates it as $\epsilon_i(f_jM)-\epsilon_i(M)+a$. Label independence in step 3.2 transfers this to any quotient containing $M,f_jM$. [step 1.1, step 2.1, step 3.2, step 4.1, step 5.1, F2, algebra]

7.1 The initial value is now fixed, not inferred from a decrement recurrence. On the vacuum, $f_i^n\mathbf1=L_n$ has $c_i=n$, so its containing length is exactly $\lambda_i$ by [F1]. Every nonvacuum simple has some positive right tail (choose the last letter of any nonzero word corner), so write $M=f_jN$ with $N=e_jM$ of lower height. Both survive whenever $M$ survives by [F1]. If $j=i$, surviving length decreases by one, right tail increases by one and $\langle h_i,\beta\rangle$ increases by two. If $j\ne i$, step 6.1 gives the change in surviving length as $\epsilon_i(M)-\epsilon_i(N)-a_{ij}$. Induction on height from the vacuum therefore yields $ v_i^\lambda(M)=\lambda_i+\epsilon_i(M)-\langle h_i,\beta\rangle$. Combining this with the independently proved formula in step 3.2 gives $J_i(M)=\epsilon_i(M)+c_i(M)-\langle h_i,\beta\rangle$. In particular the initial zero-jump test is precisely $\epsilon_i(M)+c_i(M)=\langle h_i,\beta\rangle$; its value follows from the rank-two/annihilation calculation and the vacuum base, rather than the recurrence alone. The formula is symmetric in the two ends, so the corresponding first-end jump and its decrement formula also hold. [step 3.2, step 6.1, F1, algebra]

8.1 Define the elementary crystal $B_i$ by $\operatorname{wt}(b_i(n))=n\alpha_i$, $\epsilon_i(b_i(n))=-n$, $\phi_i(b_i(n))=n$, $e_ib_i(n)=b_i(n+1)$, $f_ib_i(n)=b_i(n-1)$; other-colour epsilon and phi are $-\infty$ and other-colour operators zero. On a tensor $X\otimes Y$, epsilon is $\max(\epsilon_l(X),\epsilon_l(Y)-\langle h_l,\operatorname{wt}(X)\rangle)$; $e_l$ acts on $X$ iff $\phi_l(X)\ge\epsilon_l(Y)$ and $f_l$ acts on $X$ iff $\phi_l(X)>\epsilon_l(Y)$, otherwise on $Y$. To check the $i$-data and both branches set $s=J_i(U)=\epsilon_i(U)+\langle h_i,\operatorname{wt}(U)\rangle\ge0$. Along the first-$i$ string from $U$, the symmetric jump recurrence and step 2.1 give $\epsilon_i(M)=\epsilon_i(U)+\max(0,c-s)$. This is exactly $\max(\epsilon_i(U),c-\langle h_i,\operatorname{wt}(U)\rangle)$, the tensor epsilon. Weight is also preserved since $\operatorname{wt}(U)=\operatorname{wt}(M)+c\alpha_i$. For lowering, if $s>c$ then $J_i(M)=s-c>0$, $c_i(f_iM)=c$, and step 3.3 gives extracted factor $f_iU$; if $s\le c$ then $J_i(M)=0$, $c_i(f_iM)=c+1$ and its extracted factor is $U$. These are precisely the strict $f_i$ branches. For raising, if $s<c$ then the predecessor $(f_i^L)^{c-1}U$ has zero jump, so $e_iM=e_i^LM$, first tail $c-1$ and extracted factor $U$. If $s\ge c>0$, that predecessor has positive jump; a zero jump at $e_iM$ would force $e_iM=e_i^LM$ by step 2.1 and contradict that positive jump. Hence $c_i(e_iM)=c$ and step 3.3 applied to $e_iM$ gives extracted factor $e_iU$. When $c=0$ the same first branch holds directly. If $e_iM=0$, the epsilon formula forces $e_iU=0$ and $s\ge c$, so the tensor operator is also zero. Thus both raising branches, including equality and zero cases, agree. For $j\ne i$, step 3.3 gives the epsilon equality and both operator compatibilities; phi equality follows from epsilon and weight. Finally $U,c$ recover $M=(f_i^L)^cU$, giving injectivity. Every nonvacuum has a nonzero word corner and therefore positive first tail at its first letter, while right-tail stripping decreases height to the unique vacuum and its partial inverse recovers every lowering word. All generic $f_i$ are nonzero by [F1]. [step 2.1, step 7.1, step 3.3, F1, algebra]

9.1 Step 7.1 proves the actual surviving right lowering length in every containing first-strand quotient, including zero length and the vacuum. The linear divided restriction Serre relation is the Hom-dual of the projective Serre identity used in step 3.1; it is a statement about the exact linear $G_0$ operators, and makes no linear Serre assertion about the simple-socle operators. All containing labels and support reductions used [F2], so no new original-weight-lattice hypothesis has been imposed. Steps 2.1, 3.2 and 7.1 give every jump assertion, and step 8.1 gives strict injective elementary embeddings and lowering generation, completing the stated claims. [step 2.1, step 3.1, step 3.2, step 7.1, step 8.1, F2, F5] ∎

items.title: The categorical $\mathfrak{sl}_2$ commutator for cyclotomic KLR functors
items.statement:
Let $R^\Lambda$ be the cyclotomic KLR algebra of
[[def-cyclotomic-klr-quotient-at-a-dominant-weight]], let
$E^\Lambda_i,F^\Lambda_i$ be the functors of
[[def-cyclotomic-klr-induction-and-restriction-functors]], and read the
composites $E^\Lambda_iF^\Lambda_i$ and $F^\Lambda_iE^\Lambda_i$ as
endofunctors of $\mathrm{Mod}(R^\Lambda(\beta))$ via the weight bookkeeping
fixed there. Put $\lambda:=\Lambda-\beta$ and $q_i:=q^{d_i}$
([[def-quantum-integers-factorials-and-divided-powers-at-q-i]]).

(a) If $\langle h_i,\lambda\rangle\ge0$, there is a natural isomorphism of
endofunctors of $\mathrm{Mod}(R^\Lambda(\beta))$
$$q_i^{-2}F^\Lambda_iE^\Lambda_i\oplus\bigoplus_{k=0}^{\langle h_i,\lambda\rangle-1}q_i^{2k}\mathrm{Id}\;\cong\;E^\Lambda_iF^\Lambda_i.$$

(b) If $\langle h_i,\lambda\rangle\le0$, there is a natural isomorphism of
endofunctors of $\mathrm{Mod}(R^\Lambda(\beta))$
$$q_i^{-2}F^\Lambda_iE^\Lambda_i\;\cong\;E^\Lambda_iF^\Lambda_i\oplus\bigoplus_{k=0}^{-\langle h_i,\lambda\rangle-1}q_i^{-2k-2}\mathrm{Id}.$$

Applied to the object $R^\Lambda(\beta)$ the same computation gives an
isomorphism of graded $R^\Lambda(\beta)$-bimodules obtained from
$F^\Lambda_iE^\Lambda_iR^\Lambda(\beta)$ and
$E^\Lambda_iF^\Lambda_iR^\Lambda(\beta)$ by the displayed summands
([[def-graded-ring-module-bimodule-and-internal-shift]] for the shift
conventions).

Work throughout with $\kappa=-\tau_{\rm native}$ for every color pair. This is a graded algebra isomorphism preserving $Q$ and all first-strand monic ideals: quadratic relations have two signs, the braid defect three, and $\kappa_w=(-1)^{\ell(w)}\tau_w$. Hence model crossings are native $-\pi$ and $-Q$; changing only equal-color crossings is not allowed. Use the formal category and its explicit graded flag model from the declared suppliers. With $i$ last in a total color order, raw downward flags have shifts $s_j(m)=-2d_jm_j+\sum_{\ell>j}(-b_{j\ell})m_\ell$. A degree-$D$ raw map between word shifts $S,T$ has degree $D+T-S$. Thus a source increasing crossing $\pi$ of degree zero and its reverse multiplier $Q$ of degree $-2b_{jk}$ both have actual degree $-b_{jk}$. Basic $E_iG_j$ has the prescribed $-b_{ij}$ shifted commutation. Formal $H_i=E_i^{\rm basic}\{-d_i(1+h_{\rm input})\}$ cancels that shift: $h$ increases by $-a_{ij}$ under $G_j$ and $s_j(m-e_i)=s_j(m)+b_{ij}$. It is formal $H_i$, rather than basic $E_i$, that commutes unshiftedly with the spectator flag.

At a vertex with $r$ i roots and total monic degree $N$, put $L=C[e_1,\ldots,e_r]/(\text{factor coefficients above }N-r)$, $c_r=\prod(u-x_a)$, $p=a_i\prod Q_{ij}/t_{ij}$ and $b=p/c_r$. The i-flag algebra is $B=L[z]/b(z)$, free over the old ring on powers $0\le j<N-r$ and free over the target root-append ring on powers $0\le j\le r$. The two coefficient traces $\tau_{\rm old}$ and $\tau_{\rm new}$ extract the respective top powers in their monic remainders. Their Gram matrices in power/complementary bases are triangular with diagonal one, so they have explicit dual bases without factorial denominators. Basic $F_i=B\{-2d_i r\}\otimes-$ and basic reverse $E_i=B\otimes-$ use $\tau_{\rm new}$ and its dual bases for the first adjunction and $\tau_{\rm old}$ for the second. If $(u_a,v_a)$ are either pair of dual bases, the unit is $1\mapsto\sum_av_a\otimes u_a$ and the counit is its coefficient trace. The identities $\sum_av_a\tau(u_ax)=x$ and $\sum_a\tau(xv_a)u_a=x$ give both triangles directly. The trace-degree difference is $-2d_i(N-2r-1)=t_i(\beta)$. Source second maps are normalized by $(-1)^{N+1}=(-1)^{h+1}$, with the unit given the inverse scalar; degree-zero bubbles are one. Transporting $\kappa=-\tau$ preserves these maps and triangles, and dots/crossings inherit their actual pairing-adjoint identities.

For coherent mixed maps, let $Q_{ij}(u,y)=t_{ij}q(u,y)$ with $q$ monic and replace $p$ by $pq$. The successive i/j flags have rings modulo $b$ and $bq$; their source crossings are quotient $\pi$ and multiplication by $Q$. Monic coefficient extraction gives $\epsilon_{pq}(Qf)=t_{ij}\epsilon_p(f)$ on the one-variable power basis. On all nil-Hecke matrix entries use the ordered residue form $t_r^p(z)=(-1)^{r(N-r)}\operatorname{Res}(\Delta_r b_r\operatorname{Tr}(z)/\prod_s p(X_s))$, with $\Delta_r=\prod_{s<t}(X_s-X_t)$ and $b_r=X_1^{r-1}\cdots X_{r-1}$. It equals the integral parabolic divided-difference form: summing ordered distinct roots gives $\Delta^2$, repeated roots vanish, and the resulting integral polynomial identity specializes to every characteristic. There is no $1/r!$. For $U_r=\prod_sQ_{ij}(X_s,y)$, cancellation gives $t_r^{pq}(U_rz)=(-1)^{r(-a_{ij})}t_{ij}^r t_r^p(z)$. Perfect coefficient pairings then give the full relative identity $\pi_r\widehat\epsilon^{pq}(Q(X_{r+1},y)\operatorname{lift}z)=t_{ij}\widehat\epsilon^p(z)$ after the global second-map normalization; it holds for every matrix/coset element. Its ordinary mate is the mixed-unit identity. Native single crossings add one minus sign, while the two-sideways composites have two and retain $t_{ij}$ and $t_{ji}$. Their ordered quotient is $t_{ji}/t_{ij}$ for the i strand running SW–NE. This proves the formal crossing-mate relation without assuming a one-dimensional Hom space.

Transfer that formal relation to the actual first-strand quotient using the declared cap-off kernel supplier and PBW/bubble normal form, not rank-one detection of arbitrary map equality. Let $J$ be generated by $H_iv_\Lambda$ and $a_j(x)G_jv_\Lambda$. The marked i generator closed with dot powers forces $H(t)a_i^{\rm rev}(t)=1$; its canonical unit columns $x^k\eta$, $k<\lambda_i$, have companion polynomial exactly $a_i$. Genuine vacancy loops have index $\lambda_i+1+s$ and vanish, whereas the lower fake coefficients in the monic branch are retained. Every factor through a vacuum $H_i$ bends to an added first i strand. The cap-off supplier proves the full two-double-coset PBW reduction: no first crossing closes to that zero loop; one first crossing must be equal-color and its actual cross-and-cap sum is a unit sign times $a_i(x)$, with decorated value $a_i(x)P(x,x)$. Physical exterior factors commute with closure. Arbitrary upward whiskers of a marked $a_j$ reduce by input naturality of the mixed maps/rho; for negative h use the actual retract $\iota=\rho^{-1}j_{EF}$, $\pi=p_{EF}\rho$, $\pi\iota=1$. The branch reaching the marker is zero by the companion matrix when j=i or by mixed dot commutation and $H_iv=0$ otherwise. The finite word-object induction treats every marked whisker and every factor map. Thus $J$ meets the downward corner in exactly the ordinary first-strand ideal.

The algebraic right-append kernel agrees explicitly. Set $K_0=Se(\beta,i)/Sa(x_1)R(\beta)e(\beta,i)$ and $K_1=Se(i,\beta)/Sa(x_2)R_1(\beta)e(i,\beta)$. PBW makes them finite right $R^a(\beta)[t]$-projectives. Right multiplication $P=a(x_1)\kappa_1\cdots\kappa_n$ is bilinear; its counterpart $Q=g_n\cdots g_1$ uses the source intertwiners and satisfies $QP=\sum_\nu a_i(t)\prod_{\nu_a\ne i}Q_{i\nu_a}(t,x_a)e(\nu)$, with a unit leading scalar. Hence P is injective. The full-transfer PBW coset gives $\operatorname{im}P=\ker(K_0\to R^a(\beta+\alpha_i)e(\beta,i))$; shorter cosets lie in the prefix ideal. This is also valid ungraded for arbitrary monic $a_j$. It identifies the formal quotient's word corners with the actual cyclotomic corners in dependency order. All quotient objects are summands of finite sums of negative words: move formal H through the last downward letter by mixed commutation or the sign-correct EF retract and induct on word length, starting from $H_iv=0$. Thus the idempotent-completed formal quotient is the category of actual word projectives. Right appending is the actual induction, and its first adjoint is actual basic restriction by tensor-Hom uniqueness; the rho/dot formulas fix the second maps coherently under this same identification.

Finally evaluate each formal unit/counit on the regular algebra, which is the finite sum of word idempotent projectives. Naturality with its homogeneous right multiplications (and shifts) makes each evaluated map a homogeneous bimodule map. Their two triangle identities on the regular objects are equalities of those bimodule maps. Tensoring them with any graded module therefore gives units/counits with the same triangles on all graded modules, not only word projectives. The crossing-mate equality similarly is an equality of bimodule maps and extends by tensoring. Forget the internal degrees after arbitrary inhomogeneous monic coefficient specialization; all monic, dual-basis, residue, companion, cap-off and kernel identities remain algebraic identities. No graded highest-weight action is inferred for that deformation. At every stage the finite-dimensional/root-string supplier and projectivity/commutator suppliers are algebraic prerequisites; a symmetric/Frobenius or Grothendieck/crystal theorem is never used.

items.title: Normalized cyclotomic functors give an integrable quantum action
items.statement:
For the standard graded quotient over arbitrary $k$ and graded admissible $Q$,
let $h=\langle h_i,\Lambda-\beta\rangle$. On projective $K_0$ take
$F_i=F_i^{\mathrm{basic}}$ and $E_i=q_i^{1-h}E_i^{\mathrm{basic}}$ on input
$\beta+i$ to output $\beta$. On module $G_0$ take the KK action
$E_i=E_i^{\mathrm{basic}}$ and $F_i=q_i^{1-h}F_i^{\mathrm{basic}}$ on input
$\beta$; also the canonical action with the SAME shifts as projectives. The
torus acts on root component $\beta$ by
$K_a=q^{\langle a,\Lambda-\beta\rangle}$. Each action satisfies all mixed
relations, and $E_i,F_i$ are locally nilpotent. After scalar extension to
$\mathbb Q(q)$ these are integrable type-one $U_q(\mathfrak g)$-modules. This
does not assert a decomposition into finite-dimensional full-$\mathfrak g$
submodules and does not cover ungraded monic deformations.
items.strategy:
**Proof technique:** compute the normalized operators on the two Grothendieck
groups from the basic categorical commutator, check the mixed relations and
local nilpotence, and apply the abstract integrability lemma.

1.1 The normalized operators. Projectivity of the cyclotomic bimodules supplies exact functors preserving finite projectives, so the displayed shifts define $A$-linear operators on the graded Grothendieck groups, where $A=\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$. The torus acts on the root component $\beta$ by $K_a=q^{\langle a,\Lambda-\beta\rangle}$, and each Grothendieck element has finite root support. [F3, algebra]

2.1 The mixed relation on $K_0$. Let $h=\langle h_i,\Lambda-\beta\rangle$ at input root $\beta$. The $E_i$ in $E_iF_i$ has output root $\beta$, so its normalization contributes $q_i^{1-h}$. The $E_i$ in $F_iE_i$ has output root $\beta-\alpha_i$, whose coroot label is $h+2$, so its normalization contributes $q_i^{1-(h+2)}=q_i^{-1-h}$. Multiplying the positive basic commutator of [F1] by $q_i^{1-h}$ therefore turns its $q_i^{-2}F_i^{\mathrm{basic}}E_i^{\mathrm{basic}}$ term into precisely the normalized $F_iE_i$, and its identity terms into $\sum_{k=0}^{h-1}q_i^{1-h+2k}=[h]_i$. For $h\le0$, the negative basic branch similarly gives $F_iE_i=E_iF_i+\sum_{k=0}^{-h-1}q_i^{-1-h-2k}\mathrm{Id}$, whose sum is $[-h]_i$, so the same signed relation follows. Thus $E_iF_i-F_iE_i=[h]_i\mathrm{Id}=(K_i-K_i^{-1})/(q_i-q_i^{-1})$ on root $\beta$, with $K_i=q_i^h$; the quantum integer is integral, so no division in the coefficient ring is needed. [step 1.1, F1, algebra]

3.1 The unequal-color relation and the module actions. Write $h_i(\beta)=\langle h_i,\Lambda-\beta\rangle$ and $b_{ij}=d_i a_{ij}=(\alpha_i\mid\alpha_j)$ for $i\ne j$. At input root $\beta$, the normalization of $E_i$ in $E_iF_j$ is $q_i^{1-h_i(\beta+\alpha_j-\alpha_i)}$, whereas that in $F_jE_i$ is $q_i^{1-h_i(\beta-\alpha_i)}$. Since $h_i(\beta+\alpha_j-\alpha_i)=h_i(\beta-\alpha_i)-a_{ij}$, their ratio is $q_i^{a_{ij}}=q^{b_{ij}}$. This cancels the basic crossing factor $q^{-b_{ij}}$ in [F2], giving the normalized relation $E_iF_j=F_jE_i$. The canonical $G_0$-action has the same shifts and hence the same computations as $K_0$. For the KK $G_0$-action the shift is instead carried by $F$: its exponent on input root $\beta$ is $1-h_j(\beta)$, so the ratio between $E_iF_j$ and $F_jE_i$ is $q_j^{h_j(\beta-\alpha_i)-h_j(\beta)}=q_j^{a_{ji}}=q^{b_{ij}}$, again cancelling the basic factor. For the KK same-color relation, $E_iF_i$ has shift $q_i^{1-h}$ and $F_iE_i$ has shift $q_i^{-1-h}$, exactly as in step 2.1. Both module actions therefore satisfy the required mixed relations; restriction lowers root height and the weight labels give the toral conjugation relations. [step 2.1, F2, algebra]

4.1 Local nilpotence and integrability. By [F3], $R^\Lambda(\beta+n\alpha_i)=0$ for $n$ large, so the induction operator $F_i$ is locally nilpotent componentwise; restriction lowers height, so $E_i$ is locally nilpotent as well. The toral conjugation, mixed relations and local nilpotence are exactly the hypotheses of the abstract lemma [F3], which then proves both full symmetrizable Serre families and equips the scalar extension to $\mathbb Q(q)$ with the unique integrable type-one $U_q(\mathfrak g)$-module structure. No finite-dimensionality of full weight spaces and no ungraded monic deformation is asserted; no cyclic input from vacuum generation or the integral highest-module identification is used. [step 2.1, step 3.1, F3] ∎

items.title: The word-mirror involution of a KLR algebra and the quantum star
items.statement:
On the generic graded KLR algebra define $\rho(e(\nu))=e(\operatorname{rev}\nu)$,
$\rho(x_a)=x_{n+1-a}$, $\rho(\tau_a)=-\tau_{n-a}$. This is a degree-preserving
ALGEBRA AUTOMORPHISM with $\rho^2=1$, commuting with the generator-fixing
anti-involution $\psi$. It maps $e(\nu)Re(\eta)$ to
$e(\operatorname{rev}\nu)Re(\operatorname{rev}\eta)$. Twisting LEFT modules by
$a\cdot m=\rho(a)m$ is an equivalence and commutes with finite vector duality
and projective Hom duality. Its separated-block formula is
$\rho^*\operatorname{Ind}(M,N)\cong\operatorname{Ind}(\rho^*N,\rho^*M)$,
without a shift. Under $\gamma:U_A^-\to K_0(R)$ it induces the quantum
multiplication-reversing star, fixing every $F_i$ and $q$. The first
cyclotomic generator maps to $a_{\nu_1}(x_n)e(\operatorname{rev}\nu)$, with the
SAME original first color. Thus it identifies the first- and last-strand
quotients; preservation of the first ideal itself is not asserted in general.

items.title: Cyclotomic KLR algebras are finite-dimensional graded symmetric algebras
items.statement: For the STANDARD graded cyclotomic quotient over any degree-zero field and admissible graded real symmetrizable KLR datum, every block $B=R^\Lambda(\beta)$ is finite-dimensional, all dots are nilpotent, and $R^\Lambda(\beta+n\alpha_i)=0$ for large $n$. Put $\operatorname{def}_\Lambda(\beta)=(\Lambda,\beta)-(\beta,\beta)/2$. A nonzero block has a perfect symmetric homogeneous functional $\operatorname{tr}_\beta:B\to k$ of degree $t_\beta=-2\operatorname{def}_\Lambda(\beta)$; on a zero block perfectness is vacuous and the functional is zero. Thus $DB\cong B\{t_\beta\}$ as graded bimodules. For finite projective $P$, with $P^\#=\operatorname{HOM}_B(P,B)^\psi$, one has $D_\psi P\cong P^\#\{t_\beta\}$, so vector duality preserves projectives. This does not assert $P^\#=P$ for every shifted projective, nor self-duality of every indecomposable finite module. For arbitrary monic deformation polynomials the separate conclusion is finite-dimensional and symmetric UNGRADED, with finite root strings and monic dot annihilators; nilpotence and homogeneous trace degree are not asserted. In rank one the standard trace is the top coefficient on $k[x]/x^{\lambda_i}$ and has degree $-2d_i(\lambda_i-1)$.

The image of $1_B$ is a degree-$t_ eta$ functional; naturality identifies the induced pairing with composition. The isomorphism therefore proves perfectness, rather than assuming a nonzero diagram closure detects every ideal.
Dot and equal-color mate coherence makes this raw form cyclic on those generators. For an unequal crossing the proved oriented mixed identity is $	au(pa)=(t_{ji}/t_{ij})	au(ap)$ with NE/SW color $i$. Choose a reference word and nonzero diagonal weights $c_
u$ with $c_{s
u}(t_{ji}/t_{ij})=c_

u)$ makes the trace cyclic for every generator and hence every product. Multiplication by $c$ is invertible, preserving perfectness and degree. The symmetric pairing identifies $B\{t_ eta\}$ with $DB$. Finite-projective evaluation then gives $D_\psi P=P^\#\{t_ eta\}$. items.title: Canonical elementary crystal extraction and highest-weight survivors
items.statement:
For every real symmetrizable Cartan datum, the canonical negative-half crystal
has strict elementary embeddings
$\Psi_i(b)=\bar b\otimes b_i(-c_i(b))$, where $c_i(b)=\epsilon_i(*b)$,
$\bar b=(e_i^*)^{c_i(b)}b$, $c_i(\bar b)=0$, and every nonvacuum vertex has
positive extraction for some $i$. The negative-half reversal $*$ permutes
$B(\infty)$ without signs; this unsigned conclusion is proved from the existing
signed lattice theorem and positive highest-weight tensor residues, not
assumed. The survivors of $\pi_\lambda$ are exactly $c_i(b)\le\lambda_i$ for
all $i$; with weight $\lambda+\operatorname{wt}(b)$, inherited raising and
surviving lowering, and $\epsilon/\varphi$, they are $B(\lambda)$. Any two
lowering-generated, everywhere-lowerable negative crystals with strict
nonpositive elementary extractions and positive extraction at every nonvacuum
vertex are uniquely isomorphic by their lowering words; the proof uses finite
color cycles and terminates after a height bound. Consequently for any field
and any general homogeneous nondegenerate $Q$ of the first two lemmas, the
shift-orbit simple-module crystal is canonically $B(\infty)$, its first-strand
cyclotomic simple graph is $B(\lambda)$, and the graph labeled by
indecomposable projective COVERS $P(S)$ is the same graph under the unscaled
cover--simple pairing. Projective crystal operators here mean operators
transported on cover labels; no arbitrary $\#$-dual-of-simple identification,
generic global-basis theorem, or independent linear Kashiwara action on the
projective class is used.
items.strategy:
**Proof technique:** lift the right-string decomposition of the negative half
to lattice components, read the strict elementary embeddings off the top
residue, identify the survivors of the highest-weight projection, and use the
lattice comparison to identify the categorified simple graph.

1.1 The correctly oriented signed right-string decomposition. Put $e_i^*=*\tilde e_i*$, $f_i^*=*\tilde f_i*$ and $P_i^*=*P_i*$, where $P_i$ is the left-string projector of [F1]. Applying the anti-involution to the unique left decomposition of $*u$ gives $u=\sum_{n\ge0}v_nF_i^{(n)}$, with $v_n\in\ker(*e_i'*)$ and $v_n=q_i^{n(n-1)/2}P_i^*(*e_i'*)^nu$. In particular the divided powers are on the RIGHT. If $T_n=(e_i^*)^nu$, shifting this right decomposition gives $v_n=T_n-f_i^*T_{n+1}$; all these coefficients lie in the crystal lattice because the signed lattice theorem makes $e_i^*,f_i^*$ lattice-preserving. On its residue $e_i^*,f_i^*$ preserve the SIGNED crystal set and are partial inverses. For a residue $b$, let $c=\max\{n:(e_i^*)^nb\ne0\}$, finite by root height. Then for $n<c$ the residue of $v_n$ is zero by the partial-inverse identity, for $n=c$ it is $(e_i^*)^cb$, and for $n>c$ it is zero. Thus precisely one right-string coefficient has nonzero residue, and that top residue is a signed basis vector. This proves oriented extraction and signed uniqueness; it does not determine the sign of the extracted residue or prove the unsigned-star assertion. [F1, algebra]

2.1 Signed adaptation already determines the kernel. This calculation precedes the unsigned conclusion. By balanced uniqueness, the signed reversal of a global lift is the global lift of its signed residue. Reversing the adapted LEFT-string global basis therefore makes the saturated RIGHT ideal $U_q^-F_i^s$ the span of the global vectors whose signed right depth in step 1.1 is at least $s$; the signs do not change that span. The exact based kernel of [F2] is the sum of these right ideals at $s=\lambda_i+1$. A sum of subspaces spanned by subsets of one basis is spanned by the union of those subsets. Consequently $\pi_\lambda(b)\ne0$ precisely when every signed right depth satisfies $c_i(b)\le\lambda_i$, without presupposing unsigned star or elementary strictness. In particular, when $\lambda_i=0$ and the other coordinates exceed a fixed height bound, projection is a bijection from the positive vertices of that bound with $c_i=0$ to the corresponding highest-module vertices. For a surviving vertex, raising preserves survival: if $e_jb\ne0$ then $f_je_jb=b$, and lowering compatibility forces $\pi_\lambda(e_jb)\ne0$. Thus projection preserves every raising depth on survivors. [step 1.1, F1, F2, algebra]

2.2 Exact tensor coefficient comparison. Put $D_i=*e_i'*$. Write the part of $\Delta u$ whose second factor has degree $-n\alpha_i$ as $C_n(u)K_i^n\otimes F_i^{(n)}$. The coefficient is $C_n(u)=q_i^{n(n-1)/2}D_i^nu$. Indeed appending $F_j$ to a word gives $C_n(uF_j)=q_i^{-na_{ij}}C_n(u)F_j+\delta_{ij}[n]_iC_{n-1}(u)$, with $C_0(u)=u$ and $C_n(1)=0$ for $n>0$. The right Leibniz rule gives $D_i(uF_j)=q_i^{-a_{ij}}D_i(u)F_j+\delta_{ij}u$; iterating it gives the same recurrence for $q_i^{n(n-1)/2}D_i^n$, since $1+q_i^{-2}+\cdots+q_i^{-2(n-1)}=q_i^{-(n-1)}[n]_i$. This proves the formula on words and by linearity on the Serre quotient. Hence if $D_iv=0$ the only pure-$i$ second component of $\Delta v$ is $v\otimes1$. Also $\Delta F_i^{(r)}=\sum_{s=0}^rq_i^{-s(r-s)}F_i^{(r-s)}K_i^s\otimes F_i^{(s)}$, by expanding the two $q_i^{-2}$-commuting summands of [F4]. Choose auxiliary dominant weights with $\lambda_i=0$, $\lambda_j$ arbitrarily large for $j\ne i$, $\mu=m\Lambda_i$ and $m$ arbitrarily large. For the right decomposition $u=\sum_rv_rF_i^{(r)}$ of step 1.1, project $\Phi_{\lambda,\mu}\pi_{\lambda+\mu}(u)=\Delta u(v_\lambda\otimes v_\mu)$ onto the direct sum of second-factor weights $\mu-r\alpha_i$. Since $F_i v_\lambda=0$, the terms $s<r$ vanish and $K_i^rv_\lambda=v_\lambda$. The resulting exact field-vector identity is $\sum_r\pi_\lambda(v_r)\otimes F_i^{(r)}v_\mu$. No unsigned-star assertion has entered this coefficient computation. [step 1.1, F1, F2, F4, algebra]

3.1 Positivity of the extracted coefficient. Fix a height bound $H$ and take $m>H$ and the other $\lambda_j$ large enough that $\lambda+\mu$ projects isomorphically in degrees of height at most $H$, while $\varphi_j(x)>H$ for every first-factor vertex $x$ of those degrees and $j\ne i$. The tensor map is lattice-preserving by the grand loop and commutes with the module string operators. Its image of a positive negative-half lowering word is therefore a positive tensor-basis vertex: start at $v_\lambda\otimes v_\mu$ and apply the same lowering word, using [F2]. It is nonzero because the reverse tensor map is lattice-preserving and their composite is the identity. Throughout these bounded words the second factor stays on its pure-$i$ string. In fact for $j\ne i$ that factor has $\varepsilon_j=0$ (as $E_jF_i^{(n)}v_\mu=0$), and the large first-factor $\varphi_j$ selects the first tensor branch; the $i$-operator either acts on the first factor or advances that pure-$i$ string. Now take a lattice lift $u$ of a positive vertex $b$. Step 1.1 gives exactly one nonzero coefficient residue, at $c=c_i(b)$, equal to a signed vertex $\bar b$ with $c_i(\bar b)=0$. By step 2.1 its projection $\pi_\lambda(\bar b)$ is nonzero. The direct second-weight projection preserves the tensor lattice, so the identity of step 2.2 gives the tensor residue $\pi_\lambda(\bar b)\otimes f_i^cv_\mu$. Its positivity forces $\bar b$ to be positive, since the positive residue projection is a bijection on the $c_i=0$ survivors and a negative residue projects to its negative. Thus the actual extraction of every positive vertex has a positive first component. [step 1.1, step 2.1, step 2.2, F2, F4, algebra]

4.1 Strictness in both branches and every color. Define $\Psi_i(b)=\bar b\otimes b_i(-c)$ using the elementary crystal and abstract tensor conventions of [F5]. It is injective because signed partial inverses recover $b=(f_i^*)^c\bar b$. To check an operator, enlarge the finite height bound to include the vertex and its one-step neighbors and use the same $\lambda,\mu$ throughout. Step 3.1 identifies the positive tensor lift with $\pi_\lambda(\bar b)\otimes f_i^cv_\mu$. Projection preserves raising depths on survivors by step 2.1, so $\varepsilon_i(\pi_\lambda\bar b)=\varepsilon_i(\bar b)$ and, since $\lambda_i=0$, $\varphi_i(\pi_\lambda\bar b)=\varphi_i(\bar b)$. The second factor has $\varepsilon_i=c$. The finite tensor rule therefore sends $e_i$ to the first factor if $\varphi_i(\bar b)\ge c$, and to the second if $\varphi_i(\bar b)<c$; it sends $f_i$ to the first if $\varphi_i(\bar b)>c$, and to the second if $\varphi_i(\bar b)\le c$. These are exactly the two elementary branches, including their different equality choices. For $j\ne i$ the large first-factor $\varphi_j$ selects the first factor for both operators; the elementary factor, with $\varepsilon_j=\varphi_j=-\infty$, selects that same factor. Applying step 3.1 to the resulting neighbor and using uniqueness of the surviving first-factor lift identifies its actual extraction with this computed tensor result. If the first-factor raising is zero, both calculations give zero; lowering has no end in the half, and $m>H$ avoids the finite second-factor end. The finite tensor max formula gives $\varepsilon_i(b)=\max(\varepsilon_i(\bar b),c-\langle h_i,\mathrm{wt}(\bar b)\rangle)$ and $\varepsilon_j(b)=\varepsilon_j(\bar b)$ for $j\ne i$, because the large $\lambda_j$ suppress the second term there. Subtracting the auxiliary highest weights gives the elementary weight formula, and $\varphi=\varepsilon+\langle h,\mathrm{wt}\rangle$ gives all $\varphi$ identities. Thus $\Psi_i$ is an actual strict positive elementary embedding in every color, using only integrable tensor crystals for the finite calculation. [step 2.1, step 3.1, F2, F4, F5, algebra]

5.1 Unsigned star and positive extraction. For each positive $b$, the signed partial inverse gives $(e_i^*)^cb=\bar b>0$ and $b=(f_i^*)^c\bar b$. Applying signed extraction to each intermediate $(e_i^*)^rb$ gives the same positive top component $\bar b$ and position $c-r$. A negative intermediate residue would instead have a negative top component by linearity and step 3.1, so every intermediate is positive. Likewise, for a positive right-primitive vertex $a$ and $n\ge0$, the signed vertex $(f_i^*)^na$ has top coefficient $a$ and depth $n$, and cannot be negative because the extraction of a negative vertex has negative top coefficient. Thus the right operators preserve the positive crystal wherever nonzero. Every nonvacuum $b$ has some $c_i(b)>0$: its signed reversal has the same positive height, and its underlying positive vertex is a nonempty lowering word, hence has a nonzero raising in some color. Now induct on height. The vacuum is star-fixed; choose $i$ with $c=c_i(b)>0$. Its positive extracted $\bar b$ has smaller height, so $*\bar b$ is positive by induction. Reversing $b=(f_i^*)^c\bar b$ gives $*b=f_i^c(*\bar b)$, which is positive. Involutivity proves $*B(\infty)=B(\infty)$ without signs, and the previously defined signed depth is now exactly $\varepsilon_i(*b)$. All auxiliary computations involved only finitely many degrees and colors and preserve the original negative half, so the conclusions hold for the original real symmetrizable datum. [step 1.1, step 3.1, step 4.1, F1, F2, F4, algebra]

6.1 Survivors of the highest-weight projection. The projection $\pi_\lambda$ kills exactly the negative-half crystal vertices with $c_i(b)>\lambda_i$ for some $i$, by the signed adapted-kernel computation of step 2.1 and the unsigned conclusion of step 5.1. This is a consequence of the actual sum of based right ideals, not a presupposed elementary embedding or survivor comparison. The crystal-lattice comparison of [F2] makes the projection commute with the crystal operators modulo $q$. The survivors therefore carry weight $\lambda+\operatorname{wt}(b)$ with inherited raising and surviving lowering operators and the induced $\epsilon/\varphi$; the grand-loop and tensor-product theorems of [F2] identify the resulting crystal with $B(\lambda)$. [step 2.1, step 5.1, F1, F2]

6.2 Recognition once strict positive extractions exist. The canonical extractions have been constructed in steps 2.2–5.1; we now prove the abstract comparison used also by the categorical graph. By the abstract tensor definitions of [F5], let $C,C'$ be the negative crystals in the Statement, with unique weight-zero vacuums and extractions $x\mapsto x'\otimes b_i(-c_i(x))$, so $\mathrm{wt}(x')=\mathrm{wt}(x)+c_i(x)\alpha_i$. First, zero extraction fixes the first factor. Indeed the vacuum maps to $u\otimes b_i(0)$ by nonpositive weights and uniqueness of weight zero. Induct on height and write $x=f_jy$. If the last position of $\Psi_i(x)$ is zero, the tensor lowering rule and nonpositive last positions imply that $\Psi_i(y)$ also has last position zero and $f_j$ acted on its first factor: the second branch, possible only for $j=i$, strictly decreases that last position. By induction its first factor is $y$, so the new first factor is $f_jy=x$. This proves the claim without an extra identity hypothesis on zero extractions. Fix a finite set $I_0$ supporting the weights of two lowering words under comparison and cycle through all its colors $H$ times, where $H$ is their maximum height. Apply each successive extraction to the first factor. Its height never increases; during a whole cycle either it is already the vacuum or at least one extraction is positive: if none is positive the first factor stays fixed and has all its extractions zero, contradicting the nonvacuum hypothesis. Colors outside $I_0$ have zero extraction because the first factor's weight stays in $-Q_{+,I_0}$. Hence after $H$ cycles every vertex of height at most $H$ maps injectively into $\{u\}\otimes B_{i_N}\otimes\cdots\otimes B_{i_1}$. The resulting composite remains strict on the whole crystal, and sends its vacuum to $u\otimes b_{i_N}(0)\otimes\cdots\otimes b_{i_1}(0)$. Consequently the image of a lowering word is computed by applying that same word to this common tensor vacuum, for both $C$ and $C'$. If two words agree in $C$, their tensor images agree, so injectivity forces agreement in $C'$; the reverse follows identically. Matching lowering words therefore defines inverse strict isomorphisms, independent of paths. This finite argument proves recognition conditional on the stated strict positive extraction hypotheses, without using height termination alone as a substitute for path independence. [step 4.1, step 5.1, F5, algebra, construct]

7.1 The categorified graph. For any field and any general homogeneous nondegenerate $Q$ satisfying the hypotheses of the two one-step lemmas of [F3], the shift-orbit simple-module graph is lowering-generated with strict elementary extractions by [F3]; step 6.2 identifies it canonically with $B(\infty)$. In a first-strand cyclotomic quotient the surviving simple graph is exactly the survivor set of step 6.1, hence is $B(\lambda)$; the graph labeled by indecomposable projective covers $P(S)$ is the same graph under the unscaled cover--simple pairing of the cover-descent lemma, since the pairing matches each cover label with its simple head without rescaling. Operators on cover labels are transported from the simple graph; no arbitrary $\#$-dual-of-simple identification and no general global-basis theorem is used. [step 6.1, step 6.2, F3]

8.1 Choice bookkeeping. The argument is a chain of the inherited suppliers [F1] and [F2]; the Axiom of Choice is inherited through the grand-loop crystal-basis and highest-weight projection contracts used for the signed based kernel, positive tensor residues and survivor comparison in steps 2.1–6.1. No additional infinite choice is made in the right-string, finite auxiliary tensor, height and word computations of steps 1.1–5.1 and 7.1. [step 1.1, step 6.1, F1, F2] ∎

items.title: Cyclotomic projective covers and dualities descend through the quotient
items.statement:
Let $A=R(\beta)$ and $B=A/J$ be the standard homogeneous cyclotomic quotient.
For an indecomposable finite graded projective generic cover $P(S)$,
$B\otimes_AP(S)$ is its same-head indecomposable $B$-cover if $JS=0$, and is
zero otherwise. Every graded simple/indecomposable projective $B$-orbit arises
this way, and distinct surviving heads do not merge. Finite projective Hom
duality commutes with this base change, and finite vector duality commutes with
inflation. Thus generic normalized $\#$-self-dual covers and $D_\psi$-self-dual
simples supply unique normalized $B$-covers/simples. For these labels
$h(P,S)=\operatorname{gdim}\operatorname{HOM}_B(P,S)$ and
$T(P,S)=\operatorname{gdim}(P^\psi\otimes_BS)$ are both $\delta_{P,S}$; $T$ is
bilinear and $h$ first-bar sesquilinear. Extension induces a surjection on
projective $K_0$. No Frobenius, geometric basis or cyclotomic crystal premise
is used.
items.strategy:
**Proof technique:** apply the quotient adjunction to projective covers, control indecomposability through the local degree-zero endomorphism rings, then compare the two dualities and the two pairing forms.

1.1 Base change of projectives and covers. A finite graded projective $P$ is a retract of a finite sum of shifted copies of $A$, so $B\otimes_AP$ is a retract of a finite sum of shifted copies of $B$: it is finite graded projective. The quotient adjunction identifies $\operatorname{Hom}_A(P,B\otimes_AP')=\operatorname{Hom}_B(B\otimes_AP,B\otimes_AP')$, and every degree-zero endomorphism of $B\otimes_AP$ lifts through the canonical map $P\to B\otimes_AP$; endomorphisms preserve $JP$, so the induced map $\operatorname{End}^0_A(P)\to\operatorname{End}^0_B(B\otimes_AP)$ is a surjective ring homomorphism. If $P$ is indecomposable, its finite-dimensional local degree-zero endomorphism ring has no nontrivial idempotent, so a nonzero quotient has none either: $B\otimes_AP$ is zero or indecomposable. If $JS=0$, the old cover map factors through $P/JP$ and remains essential (a submodule of $B\otimes_AP$ mapping onto $S$ pulls back to a submodule of $P$ mapping onto $S$; essentiality of the old cover makes it all of $P$), so $B\otimes_AP$ is the projective cover of $S$ with the same head. If $JS\ne0$ and $B\otimes_AP\ne0$, finite dimension [F3] supplies a simple quotient, which must be the unique head $S$; as a $B$-module that quotient is annihilated by $J$, forcing $JS=0$ and contradicting the assumption, so $B\otimes_AP=0$. [F1, F3]

2.1 Every $B$-orbit arises and heads do not merge. Every simple $B$-module is a simple $A$-module by inflation, and its descended cover $B\otimes_AP(S)$ is a nonzero cover, so every $B$-simple/projective orbit arises this way. Distinct surviving heads remain distinct after quotienting because an isomorphism of the descended covers induces an isomorphism of their simple heads as $B$-modules, hence also as $A$-modules after inflation; hence the surviving projective-cover shift orbits cannot merge, and extension of scalars is surjective on projective $K_0$. [step 1.1, F1]

3.1 Dualities. For finite $P$, evaluation on shifted free modules and restriction to retracts identifies $\operatorname{HOM}_B(B\otimes_AP,B)=\operatorname{HOM}_A(P,A)\otimes_AB$, and applying the generator-fixing anti-involution $\psi$ gives $(B\otimes_AP)^\#=B\otimes_AP^\#$. Inflation does not change the finite vector duality $D_\psi$ of a simple, since the underlying vector space and the $\psi$-action are unchanged. The choice-free normalization clauses of [F2] therefore carry the unique $\#$-self-dual generic covers and $D_\psi$-self-dual simples to unique normalized $B$-covers and simples. [step 2.1, F2]

4.1 The two pairings. For normalized labels, $h(P,S)=\operatorname{gdim}\operatorname{HOM}_B(P,S)=q^a$ in a single shift $a$ because $\operatorname{End}(S)=k$ absolutely, while distinct heads give zero; assigning the simple's shift makes $h=\delta_{P,S}$. Similarly $T(P,S)=\operatorname{gdim}(P^\psi\otimes_BS)=\delta_{P,S}$ by finite-projective evaluation and $D(P^\psi\otimes S)=\operatorname{HOM}_B(P,D_\psi S)$ for evaluation of a tensor functional; $T$ is bilinear in the two arguments and $h(P,M)=T(P^\#,M)$ is first-bar sesquilinear. Extension of scalars induces the surjection on projective $K_0$ by step 2.1. No Frobenius, geometric basis or cyclotomic crystal statement is used. [step 2.1, step 3.1, F2] ∎

items.title: Cyclotomic diagram duality and graded module duals
items.statement: For the standard graded quotient $B=R^\Lambda(\beta)$, $\psi$ is the descended anti-involution fixing $e(\nu),x_a,\tau_a$. For a finite module $M$ define $D_\psi M=\operatorname{HOM}_k(M,k)^\psi$, with $(af)(m)=f(\psi(a)m)$. For a finite graded PROJECTIVE $P$ define instead $P^\#=\operatorname{HOM}_B(P,B)^\psi$. Both reverse internal shifts and are involutive on their respective domains. They are DIFFERENT dualities; Hom duality is not applied to a nonprojective simple to produce its cover. By [[lem-cyclotomic-projective-covers-and-dualities-descend-through-the-quotient]], each simple orbit has a unique $D_\psi$-self-dual representative $S$, and its unique normalized cover $P$ with $\operatorname{Hom}^0(P,S)=k$ is $\#$-self-dual. These are the normalizations in the based statements. No self-dual shift is asserted for every indecomposable finite module. The symmetric theorem additionally gives $D_\psi P\cong P^\#\{-2\operatorname{def}_\Lambda(\beta)\}$; it does not change the canonical projective normalization.
items.strategy: The cyclotomic ideal is $\psi$-stable because its individual first-strand polynomial generators are fixed. Finite vector-space evaluation proves the double $D_\psi$ identity. Evaluation on shifted free modules, then finite retracts, proves the double projective Hom-dual identity. Quotient Hom basechange carries generic normalized projective covers to their nonzero normalized cyclotomic covers, and inflation carries the normalized vector-dual simples unchanged. The quotient-cover lemma proves the normalizations and the unscaled pairing without a Frobenius premise. The trace theorem relates the two dualities only afterward. In rank one $B=k[x]/x^\lambda$, $B^\#=B$ but $D_\psi B=B\{-2d_i(\lambda-1)\}$, illustrating the distinction.

items.title: The vacuum projective is a highest-weight generator
items.statement:
For the standard graded quotient, $1_\Lambda=[k]\in K_0(R^\Lambda(0))$ is a
nonzero highest-weight vector of weight $\Lambda$ for the normalized action.
Every finite projective is a finite retract of a sum of shifted word
projectives $P_\nu=R^\Lambda(\beta)e(\nu)$, and
$[P_\nu]=F_{\nu_n}\cdots F_{\nu_1}1_\Lambda$ for right append. The stronger
integral generation statement is by DIVIDED words: the classes
$F_{i_r}^{(a_r)}\cdots F_{i_1}^{(a_1)}1_\Lambda$ span $K_0(R^\Lambda)$ over
$A$. Thus $U_A^-1_\Lambda=K_0(R^\Lambda)$. The retract statement alone is not
claimed to make ordinary word classes an $A$-spanning set.
items.strategy:
**Proof technique:** check the vacuum's highest-weight property directly, realise every finite projective as a retract of word projectives, and transfer divided generation from the generic negative half through the quotient.

1.1 The vacuum is a nonzero highest-weight vector. The rank-zero block is $R^\Lambda(0)=k$, so $1_\Lambda=[k]$ is nonzero; restriction from root zero has zero target, so $E_i1_\Lambda=0$ for every $i$; and the torus acts on the root-zero component by $q^{\langle a,\Lambda\rangle}$, so its weight is $\Lambda$. [F1]

2.1 Word projectives and retracts. The finitely many word idempotents of a root block sum to its unit, so the regular module is the sum of the corresponding word projectives and every finite projective is a retract of a finite sum of shifted copies. The append bimodule sends the word $\nu$ to $\nu i$, and since operators in a composite act from right to left, $[P_\nu]=F_{\nu_n}\cdots F_{\nu_1}1_\Lambda$. This is a statement about retracts of ordinary word projectives; it does not by itself make ordinary word classes an $A$-spanning set. [step 1.1, F2]

3.1 Divided generation. The quotient-cover lemma [F3] makes extension of scalars surjective on split $K_0$, so it suffices to generate the generic $K_0$ by extensions of divided words. The generic negative-half categorification identifies generic $K_0$ with $U_A^-$ and its divided-power projectives with the divided generators; their extensions are the cyclotomic divided functors applied to the vacuum, so the classes $F_{i_r}^{(a_r)}\cdots F_{i_1}^{(a_1)}1_\Lambda$ span $K_0(R^\Lambda)$ over $A$. This does not divide by a quantum factorial: $F_i^a=[a]_{q_i}!F_i^{(a)}$ has a generally nonunit coefficient, which is exactly why the stronger generation statement must use divided words. Combining this generation with the independent normalized-action result of [[lem-cyclotomic-normalized-functors-give-an-integrable-quantum-action]] gives $U_A^-1_\Lambda=K_0(R^\Lambda)$ without a circular appeal to the integral highest-weight theorem. [step 2.1, F3] ∎

items.title: Cyclotomic KLR functors define an integrable quantum action on $K_0$ and $G_0$
items.statement:
For the STANDARD graded cyclotomic quotient over any field and any real symmetrizable Cartan datum with admissible graded KLR parameters, put $A=\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$, $h_i(\beta)=\langle h_i,\Lambda-\beta\rangle$, and $q_i=q^{d_i}$. On projective $K_0$ use $F_i=F_i^{\rm basic}$ and $E_i|_\beta=q_i^{-1-h_i(\beta)}E_i^{\rm basic}$; on module $G_0$ use either the SAME canonical normalization, or the Kang--Kashiwara normalization $E_i^{\rm KK}=E_i^{\rm basic}$, $F_i^{\rm KK}|_\beta=q_i^{1-h_i(\beta)}F_i^{\rm basic}$. In all cases $K_i|_\beta=q_i^{h_i(\beta)}$. These operators satisfy the full quantum mixed and Serre relations and are locally nilpotent; their scalar extensions to $\mathbb Q(q)$ are integrable weight modules. No decomposition into finite-dimensional full-$\mathfrak g$ submodules is asserted in affine or indefinite type.
The tensor pairing $T_\beta(P,M)=\mathrm{gdim}(P^\psi\otimes_{R^\Lambda(\beta)}M)$ is $A$-BILINEAR and weightwise perfect in normalized projective-cover/simple bases. The Hom pairing $h(P,M)=\mathrm{gdim}\operatorname{HOM}(P,M)$ instead satisfies $h(P,M)=T(P^\#,M)$ and is first-bar-sesquilinear. For $T$, projective $E_i$ is adjoint to module $F_i^{\rm KK}$ and projective $F_i$ to module $E_i^{\rm KK}$. The two module actions are conjugate by the weight rescaling $q^{\operatorname{def}_\Lambda(\beta)}$, where $\operatorname{def}_\Lambda(\beta)=(\Lambda,\beta)-(\beta,\beta)/2$.
items.strategy:
1. The normalized-action supplier combines the actual same-color categorical decomposition and unequal-color mixed crossings with finite root strings. For $E_i$ applied to input root $\beta+\alpha_i$ its exponent is $-1-h_i(\beta+\alpha_i)=1-h_i(\beta)$, exactly the target-weight normalization. Its general rank-one Hom-envelope proof gives every symmetrizable Serre relation without a rank-two finite-orbit assumption.
2. Tensor products of finite modules are finite, hence $T$ has Laurent-polynomial values. The quotient-cover lemma gives absolutely simple normalized heads and $T(P(S),S')=\delta_{S,S'}$, proving weightwise perfectness. Shifting either tensor factor multiplies by the same $q$-power; this is bilinearity, whereas finite-projective evaluation identifies $\operatorname{HOM}(P,M)$ with $(P^\#)^\psi\otimes M$, giving the different Hom convention.
3. For the corner $A_\beta\to eB_{\beta+i}e$, associativity gives $T_B(FP,M)=T_A(P,EM)$ for the BASIC functors. The generator-fixing anti-involution flips balanced tensors, so $T_B(P,FM)=T_A(EP,M)$ as well: the corner factors become $eB$ and $Be$ in opposite order and multiplication gives the evaluation isomorphism. Multiplying the second identity by $q_i^{1-h_i(\beta)}$ gives the first normalized adjoint statement; the first identity gives the other. This uses neither the Frobenius theorem nor the highest-weight $K_0$ theorem.
4. Adding $i$ changes defect by $d_i(h_i(\beta)-1)$. Consequently multiplication by $q^{\operatorname{def}_\Lambda(\beta)}$ conjugates the canonical module action to the KK action in both directions. The weight action is unchanged. All assertions here are about the standard homogeneous quotient, not arbitrary monic deformations.

items.title: The cyclotomic projective $K_0$ is the integral highest-weight module
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice [[def-axiom-of-choice]]. For the standard homogeneous graded quotient over any field, with arbitrary real symmetrizable Cartan datum and admissible graded KLR parameters, there is a unique $U_A$-module isomorphism $\phi:K_0(\mathrm{Proj}\,R^\Lambda)\to V_A(\Lambda)$ sending $1_\Lambda$ to $v_\Lambda$ and intertwining all normalized $E_i,F_i,K_i$ and divided powers. In particular $K_0$ is free over $A$. On the NEGATIVE half the vacuum map has exact kernel
$$\ker(U_A^-\to K_0(R^\Lambda))=\sum_{i\in I}\sum_{s>\lambda_i}U_A^-F_i^{(s)}.$$
This is the integral negative-half presentation; neither a full-$U_A$ quotient by only $F_i^{(\lambda_i+1)}$ nor invertibility of divided-power factorials is asserted.
For projectives, the tensor form $T(P,Q)=\mathrm{gdim}(P^\psi\otimes Q)$ transports to the highest-weight contravariant form normalized by $(v_\Lambda,v_\Lambda)=1$ and $\sigma(F_i)=q_i^{-1}K_iE_i$, $\sigma(E_i)=q_iF_iK_i^{-1}$, $\sigma(K_i)=K_i$. It is not the generic negative-half Lusztig form with a newly alleged radical.
items.strategy:
**Proof technique:** factor the divided vacuum map through the exact integral highest-weight presentation, prove it is an isomorphism by rational simplicity and the torsion-free source lattice, and identify the tensor form by its actual corner adjunction and normalization.

**Given:** The data of F1–F4, with AC inherited through the declared generic and quantum highest-weight suppliers.

1.1 By F1 the map $U_A^-\to K_0(R^\Lambda)$, $u\mapsto u1_\Lambda$, is surjective. For every $s>\lambda_i$, the staircase idempotent in F3 is divisible on the left by $x_1^{\lambda_i}$, since $s-1\ge\lambda_i$, and therefore is zero in the standard quotient. The generator-fixing anti-involution preserves its cyclotomic ideal, so the dual projector defining the divided-power projective is zero as well. Hence $F_i^{(s)}1_\Lambda=0$ without dividing by a quantum factorial. All translates $U_A^-F_i^{(s)}$ therefore lie in its kernel. The exact integral projection presentation in F3 gives a well-defined surjective $A$-linear map $f:V_A(\Lambda)\to K_0(R^\Lambda)$ sending $v_\Lambda$ to $1_\Lambda$ and every divided word to the corresponding divided-functor class. [F1, F3, construct, algebra]

1.2 The anti-involution identifies $P^\psi\otimes Q$ with $Q^\psi\otimes P$ by interchanging the factors, so the projective tensor form $T$ is symmetric and $A$-bilinear. Different root blocks pair by zero. The basic corner identities of F2 give $T(F_iP,Q)=T(P,E_i^{\rm basic}Q)$ and $T(E_i^{\rm basic}P,Q)=T(P,F_iQ)$. At input $\beta+\alpha_i$ and output $\beta$, put $h=\langle h_i,\Lambda-\beta\rangle$. Projective $E_i=q_i^{1-h}E_i^{\rm basic}$ and $q_i^{-1}K_iE_i=q_i^{h-1}E_i=E_i^{\rm basic}$ on this target. Thus the first identity is $T(F_iP,Q)=T(P,\sigma(F_i)Q)$. [F2, F4, algebra]


1.3 The integral positive operators are defined as well. On $n$-fold basic restriction the last $n$ equal-color dots and crossings give a nil-Hecke action commuting with the target algebra. Its graded matrix-column decomposition in F3 expresses this restriction as $[n]_i!$ shifted copies of an idempotent summand, with the symmetric centering of the polynomial column. Restriction preserves finite projectives by F2, so this summand is finite projective. Multiplying it by the integral grading shift from the $n$ successive $E_i$ normalizations realizes the rational operator $E_i^n/[n]_i!$ on $K_0$; thus it preserves $K_0$ without inverting the factorial in $A$. Negative divided powers are realized by the analogous induction idempotents of F3. A toral binomial acts on an integral weight by $\prod_{s=1}^t[m+c-s+1]_i/[s]_i$. For $m+c\ge0$ this is the integral Gaussian binomial (or zero), and for $m+c<0$ it is $(-1)^t\binom{-(m+c)+t-1}{t}_i$, again integral by [[lem-quantum-pascal-recurrence-and-gaussian-integrality]]. Hence the full $U_A$ acts on $K_0$; its relations follow from the rational action because the cover basis in F4 makes $K_0$ torsion-free. [F2, F3, F4, F5, algebra]


2.1 The quotient-cover bases in F4 make $K_0$ free over $A$; in particular its nonzero vacuum stays nonzero after tensoring with $\mathbb Q(q)$. By F2 the rationalized target is an integrable cyclic highest-weight module of weight $\Lambda$. The universality and ordinary simplicity in F3 identify it with $V(\Lambda)$ by the unique map preserving the highest vector. This map is the rationalization of $f$, since both agree on every divided word. Thus $f$ becomes an isomorphism after localization. [F2, F3, F4, step 1.1, algebra]

3.1 An element $z\in\ker f$ maps to zero on localization, so some nonzero $a\in A$ kills $z$. The source $V_A(\Lambda)$ is an actual submodule of the vector space $V(\Lambda)$ over the fraction field, by F3, and is consequently torsion-free. Hence $z=0$, proving $f$ injective. Its inverse $\phi$ is the required integral isomorphism; the original vacuum map has exactly the integral projection kernel in the Statement. The rational isomorphism intertwines all normalized positive, negative and toral operators. Each difference of their integral operator maps has zero localization, and the target $K_0$ is torsion-free by F4, so the equality holds integrally, including the actual divided powers. Uniqueness follows from divided-word generation. [F1, F3, F4, step 2.1, algebra]

4.1 For the second identity, take $P$ at root $\beta+\alpha_i$ and $Q$ at root $\beta$. Its normalization yields $T(E_iP,Q)=q_i^{1-h}T(P,F_iQ)$. On $Q$, $q_iF_iK_i^{-1}=q_i^{1-h}F_i$, so this is $T(E_iP,Q)=T(P,\sigma(E_i)Q)$. The torus is scalar on each root component and preserves its label, giving toral contravariance. The vacuum tensor product is $k$, of norm one. Transported by $\phi$, these identities and symmetry give exactly the normalized highest-weight contravariant form; uniqueness in F4 identifies it. This uses the highest-weight form, rather than the generic negative-half form or a supposed new radical of that form. [F2, F4, step 3.1, step 1.2, algebra]

5.1 Steps 1.1, 2.1 and 3.1 prove the unique integral highest-weight isomorphism and its exact divided right-power kernel in the full stated general-field/general-Cartan scope. Steps 1.2 and 4.1 prove the tensor-form assertion. Projective-cover shift orbits give the independent free $A$-basis, without treating all divided words as a basis or making a quantum factorial invertible. AC is inherited only through the declared generic categorification and quantum highest-weight suppliers; the localization, torsion-free kernel and finite corner computations introduce no further choice.
