items.title: The cyclotomic module $G_0$ is the restricted dual integral highest-weight module
items.statement:
For the same standard homogeneous general-field/general-Cartan parameters as the integral projective theorem, the tensor pairing $T(P,M)=\mathrm{gdim}(P^\psi\otimes M)$ is weightwise perfect and $A$-bilinear, with normalized cover/simple dual bases. Its associated map
$$\Psi_{\rm can}:G_0(R^\Lambda)\longrightarrow V_A(\Lambda)^\vee=\bigoplus_\beta\operatorname{Hom}_A(V_A(\Lambda)_{\Lambda-\beta},A),\qquad \Psi_{\rm can}(M)(\phi(P))=T(P,M)$$
is an isomorphism to the RESTRICTED weight dual, identified inside $V(\Lambda)$ using the highest-weight contravariant form. It intertwines the CANONICAL module action having the same normalization as projective $K_0$, and sends normalized simple classes to the form-dual projective basis. The KK module action is also sound, but its intertwiner is $\Psi_{\rm KK}|_\beta=q^{\operatorname{def}_\Lambda(\beta)}\Psi_{\rm can}|_\beta$. Thus an unrescaled KK identification is not asserted to send simples to the upper global basis. The Hom pairing is instead first-bar-sesquilinear, $h(P,M)=T(P^\#,M)$; this does not alter the bilinear tensor-dual identification.
items.strategy:
1. Finite blocks have finitely many absolutely simple graded shift orbits and normalized projective covers, by the quotient-cover lemma. Exactness of projective tensor pairing and the unscaled diagonal values give perfectness over $A$ on each weight. Consequently $G_0$ is free with these simple classes, and the functional map is an isomorphism to the weightwise dual of $K_0$. Take the DIRECT SUM over weights, not the full unrestricted product dual.
2. Transport $K_0$ by $\phi$. Its tensor form is the actual highest-weight contravariant form with $\sigma(F_i)=q_i^{-1}K_iE_i$. From tensor adjunction, $T(P,F_i^{\rm basic}M)=T(E_i^{\rm basic}P,M)=T(\sigma(F_i)P,M)$; the analogous normalized $E_i$ identity is $T(P,E_i^{\rm can}M)=T(\sigma(E_i)P,M)$. These are precisely the restricted contravariant-dual action. Thus $\Psi_{\rm can}$ intertwines, without identifying an ordinary transpose action with the wrong quantum normalization.
3. The defect difference computed in the action theorem shows that $q^{\operatorname{def}_\Lambda(\beta)}\Psi_{\rm can}$ intertwines KK $E$ and $F$. In rank one $\lambda=2$, the middle form norm is $1+q^2$, so the canonical upper vector is $Fv/(1+q^2)$ and its $E$ image is $q^{-1}v$. This matches $E^{\rm can}=q^{-1}\mathrm{Res}$, whereas KK $E=\mathrm{Res}$ sends the middle simple to the vacuum without that factor; the defect rescaling accounts for it.
4. On normalized covers $P^\#=P$, so $h$ and $T$ have the same diagonal simple values. On arbitrary shifted classes their scalar rules differ exactly as stated. This establishes the duality claim with the genuine restricted lattice and both correct module actions.

items.title: Simple and indecomposable-projective crystals agree with $B(\Lambda)$
items.statement: For the standard homogeneous cyclotomic quotient over any field with the general real symmetrizable datum and graded KLR parameters, let $\mathcal B_\Lambda$ be the normalized $D_\psi$-self-dual simple classes. Set $\mathrm{wt}(S)=\Lambda-\beta$, $\varepsilon_i(S)=\max\{r:(E_i^{\rm basic})^rS\ne0\}$ and $\varphi_i(S)=\varepsilon_i(S)+\langle h_i,\mathrm{wt}(S)\rangle$. For $\varepsilon_i>0$, define $\widetilde e_iS$ by the unique simple isomorphism type in the socle of one-step right restriction, with its unique self-dual normalization; define $\widetilde f_iS$ by the simple head of right induction when nonzero, otherwise zero. The one-step socle/head is one shifted copy, not a quantum-factorial multiplicity. These data form a crystal canonically isomorphic to $B(\Lambda)$, with vacuum sent to $u_\Lambda$. The normalized indecomposable projectives carry the same crystal by their normalized simple heads and covers. The projective graph here is explicitly transported from these labels, rather than obtained by applying linear Kashiwara operators to an unspecified projective basis. The highest-weight quotient has simple survivors exactly when $\varepsilon_i^{\rm LEFT}(S)\le\lambda_i$ for every $i$.
items.strategy:
1. Inflate a cyclotomic simple to the generic algebra. The one-step supplier proves the actual unique head/socle and rank-one multiplicities through the nil-Hecke matrix/corner description; its first-dot index identifies the FIRST-strand ideal criterion with $\varepsilon_i^{\rm LEFT}\le\lambda_i$. This argument uses finite-dimensional nilpotent-dot simples and works over the original field, including positive characteristic.
2. The two-color supplier proves the full general-$Q$ jump formula and strict elementary embeddings from actual shuffle filtrations, divided restriction multiplicities and explicit rank-two operators. The linear Serre relation is applied in $G_0$, not to a nonlinear simple operator. It establishes the generic crystal extraction hypotheses in every real symmetrizable type; no ADE-only or finite-rank-two-orbit argument replaces them.
3. Apply the canonical elementary-extraction/highest-weight-survivor supplier. Its positive highest-weight tensor models and unsigned star identification give the generic $B(\infty)$ labeling by RIGHT operators and identify the left-survivor subset with the canonical $B(\Lambda)$ under $\pi_\Lambda$. It proves connectedness from the vacuum, strictness and the truncation of induction at the string endpoint. If an auxiliary primitive-coroot datum is needed for sufficiently large containing weights, it has the same $A,D,Q$ and does not change the KLR algebras. Thus the displayed weight, epsilon and phi are precisely the highest-weight crystal functions.
4. The quotient-cover lemma identifies normalized covers with their simple heads bijectively, with diagonal tensor pairing. Transfer the simple arrows through this bijection. This proves the projective crystal statement and its normalized labeling without using the later lower/upper global-basis conclusions. Choice is inherited only through the declared abstract crystal/balanced-lift suppliers in the extraction step.

items.title: Cyclotomic extension of scalars respects the based quotient
items.statement:
Assume the full symmetric normalized-$d_i=1$, characteristic-zero,
loopless-quiver geometric-parameter scope of the generic global theorem, and
the STANDARD homogeneous first-strand cyclotomic quotient with RIGHT append.
Let $\gamma:U_A^-\to K_0(R)$ be the approved generic categorification and
$\phi:K_0(R^\Lambda)\to V_A(\Lambda)$ the vacuum-normalized integral
isomorphism. Then the raw extension $q_\Lambda(P)=R^\Lambda\otimes_RP$
satisfies
$$\phi[q_\Lambda(P)]=\pi_\Lambda\bigl(*(\gamma^{-1}[P])\bigr).$$
Composing extension with the generic mirror twist gives $\pi_\Lambda$ without
star. For $b\in B(\infty)$ and the generic normalized indecomposable projective
$P_b$ with $\gamma^{-1}[P_b]=G^-(b)$, raw extension is zero or a SINGLE
normalized indecomposable cyclotomic projective; its image is
$\pi_\Lambda G^-(b^*)$, which is zero or $G^-_\Lambda(\pi_\Lambda b^*)$. The
surviving cover orbits do not merge, and every normalized cyclotomic cover is
obtained. In RIGHT-simple labels $c$, the generic FIRST-recursion theorem gives
$\gamma^{-1}[P(S_c)]=G^-(c^*)$, so raw extension sends it to
$G^-_\Lambda(\pi_\Lambda c)$; these are exactly the crystal-compatible
survivor labels of the preceding theorem. The claim is for indecomposable
projectives, not every finite projective quotient.
items.strategy:
**Proof technique:** compare the side conventions on divided words, use the
mirror twist to convert star into the identity, and read survival and
non-merging off the cover-descent lemma.

1.1 The raw extension map on divided words. Right append sends a word $\nu_1\cdots\nu_n$ to $F_{\nu_n}\cdots F_{\nu_1}v_\Lambda$, whereas the generic multiplication convention assigns $F_{\nu_1}\cdots F_{\nu_n}$; on actual divided word classes the map is therefore $\pi_\Lambda\circ*$. Their $A$-span is all generic $K_0$ by [F1], so this determines the map integrally, giving $\phi[q_\Lambda(P)]=\pi_\Lambda(*(\gamma^{-1}[P]))$; composing with the generic mirror twist of [F2], which supplies exactly $*$ and commutes with projective Hom duality, gives $\pi_\Lambda$ without star. [F1, F2]

1.2 Positive star on the global basis. The generic mirror equivalence of [F2] preserves indecomposability and commutes with projective Hom duality, hence permutes the normalized generic covers. Once the generic global theorem in [F1] is instantiated, their classes are exactly the positive lower global vectors. Its induced quantum star therefore permutes these vectors with positive sign: $*G^-(b)=G^-(b^*)$. This is a consequence of the generic global theorem used here, not an input to its geometric or sign proof. [F1, F2]

2.1 Survival and non-merging. For a surviving normalized generic simple $S$, quotient Hom base change in the cover-descent lemma [F3] sends its normalized projective cover to the cyclotomic normalized cover, commutes with $\#$, and preserves its unscaled head pairing; if its simple is killed, the quotient is zero, because any nonzero finite quotient of the cover has a simple head and adjunction would produce a surviving generic head of the original cover. Thus raw extension of a generic normalized indecomposable projective is zero or a single normalized indecomposable cyclotomic projective, and distinct surviving heads do not merge; the image is $\pi_\Lambda G^-(b^*)$ respectively $G^-_\Lambda(\pi_\Lambda b^*)$ under the projections of [F1]. [step 1.1, step 1.2, F1, F3]

3.1 RIGHT-simple labels. The FIRST-block coefficient-$1$ expansion and LEFT-string ideal equality of [F4] identify the maximal FIRST-block partition of each generic cover with the adapted LEFT-string partition of its lower global vector. The one-step simple recursion increases this FIRST-string position by one; the adapted quantum recursion does the same. Induction on lowering paths from the vacuum therefore identifies the FIRST-end simple label with the ordinary canonical label. The mirror equivalence exchanges FIRST and RIGHT head/socle shift orbits, fixes the vacuum and induces star on the normalized cover class, so in the canonical RIGHT-simple label $c$ the equality is $\gamma^{-1}[P(S_c)]=G^-(c^*)$. The raw extension formula of step 1.1 cancels the two stars and sends it to $G^-_\Lambda(\pi_\Lambda c)$, with exactly the survivor label of [F3]. Every normalized cyclotomic cover is obtained because every cyclotomic simple inflates to a generic simple whose cover descends. The Axiom of Choice is inherited through the generic global-basis and quantum-projection contracts of [F1] and the canonical-extraction supplier of [F3]; no other step uses infinite choice. The claim concerns indecomposable projectives, not every finite projective quotient. [step 1.2, step 2.1, F1, F2, F3, F4] ∎

items.title: Self-dual indecomposable cyclotomic projectives give the lower global basis
items.statement:
For a symmetric Cartan datum normalized by $d_i=1$, over any
characteristic-zero field, and the SAME finite loopless quiver with arbitrary
edge multiplicities and $Q_{ij}=(-1)^{h_{ij}}(u-v)^{h_{ij}+h_{ji}}$ as the
generic global theorem, use the STANDARD homogeneous first-strand quotient and
RIGHT append. The vacuum-normalized isomorphism
$\phi:K_0(\mathrm{Proj}\,R^\Lambda)\to V_A(\Lambda)$ maps the classes of
normalized $\#$-self-dual indecomposable cyclotomic projectives bijectively
onto the lower global basis. The normalization is by projective HOM duality and
normalized simple heads, not by finite vector duality or a half-trace shift.
The projective with RIGHT crystal label $c\in B(\Lambda)$ maps to
$G^-_\Lambda(c)$. Every such projective is the surviving extension of a
generic normalized cover, with the raw map $\pi_\Lambda\circ*$ and the
FIRST/RIGHT label cancellation proved in the based-quotient lemma. The
uniqueness is at the level of normalized indecomposable projective isomorphism
classes; this is not an assertion that its generic lift is unique. No
arbitrary-parameter based extension is asserted.
items.strategy:
**Proof technique:** map each normalized cyclotomic cover to its based-quotient
class, show injectivity by the free normalized basis, and show surjectivity by
lifting lower global vectors through the generic theorem.

1.1 Cover classes land on lower global vectors. By [F1] all normalized cyclotomic covers are precisely the nonzero extensions of normalized generic covers, with distinct surviving simple heads; the based-quotient lemma sends each such class to a single positive lower global vector of $V_A(\Lambda)$, with no grading ambiguity because Hom base change preserves the $\#$-normalization and the degree-zero head pairing. [F1]

2.1 Surjectivity. Conversely the quantum global projection theorem [F2] supplies a generic global vector lifting every lower global vector of $V_A(\Lambda)$, and the generic theorem supplies its normalized generic cover; mirroring if necessary to use the raw first/right convention, its extension has that nonzero class and is a normalized indecomposable cover. Hence the assignment is surjective onto the lower basis. [step 1.1, F2]

3.1 Bijectivity and labels. The integral $K_0$ isomorphism and its free normalized projective basis make the assignment injective; the RIGHT crystal label identification of [F3] shows that the projective with RIGHT label $c\in B(\Lambda)$ maps to $G^-_\Lambda(c)$, with the FIRST/RIGHT label cancellation proved in the based-quotient lemma. The uniqueness is at the level of normalized indecomposable projective isomorphism classes, not of generic lifts, and no arbitrary-parameter based extension is asserted. The Axiom of Choice is inherited through the generic global-basis and projection contracts of [F2]. [step 2.1, F1, F2, F3] ∎

items.title: Self-dual simple cyclotomic modules give the upper global basis
items.statement:
In exactly the symmetric normalized-$d_i=1$, characteristic-zero, loopless
arbitrary-multiedge geometric-parameter regime of the lower projective theorem,
the CANONICAL restricted-dual identification
$\Psi_{\mathrm{can}}:G_0(R^\Lambda)\to V_A(\Lambda)^\vee$ maps normalized
$D_\psi$-self-dual simple classes bijectively to the upper global basis,
form-dual to the lower projective basis under the actual highest-weight
contravariant form. A simple and its normalized projective COVER have the same
$B(\Lambda)$ label; this is the cover/simple correspondence, not projective Hom
duality applied to a simple. Canonical $G_0$ operators have the same projective
normalization. The alternative KK module action remains valid, but its
intertwiner is
$\Psi_{\mathrm{KK}}=q^{\operatorname{def}_\Lambda(\beta)}
\Psi_{\mathrm{can}}$ on root $\beta$ and sends a simple to that defect-rescaled
upper vector. The unrescaled upper-basis claim is made only for
$\Psi_{\mathrm{can}}$.
items.strategy:
## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The geometric-parameter regime of the lower projective theorem, the
normalized $D_\psi$-self-dual simples and normalized covers, and the two
restricted-dual identifications.

[F1] The quotient-cover pairing
([[lem-cyclotomic-projective-covers-and-dualities-descend-through-the-quotient]]):
$T(P(S),S')=\delta_{S,S'}$ in normalized bases.

[F2] The lower projective theorem
([[thm-self-dual-indecomposable-cyclotomic-klr-projectives-give-the-lower-global-basis]]):
$\phi(P(S))$ is the lower global vector with the same crystal label.

[F3] The integral projective and $G_0$ identifications
([[thm-cyclotomic-klr-projective-k-zero-is-the-integral-highest-weight-module]],
[[thm-cyclotomic-klr-module-g-zero-is-the-dual-integral-highest-weight-module]])
and the upper/lower duality and crystal compatibility
([[thm-upper-and-lower-global-bases-are-dual-and-crystal-compatible]],
[[def-upper-global-basis-by-the-contravariant-form]],
[[def-cyclotomic-klr-diagram-duality-and-graded-module-duals]]).

## Proof

**Proof technique:** pair the normalized simple functional against the lower
basis, identify it with the form-dual lower functional, and apply the
upper/lower duality theorem; then compare the two normalizations.

1.1 The functional $\Psi_{\mathrm{can}}(S)$. By [F1] the pairing is diagonal in normalized bases, and by [F2] the class $\phi(P(S))$ is the lower global vector with the same crystal label; therefore $\Psi_{\mathrm{can}}(S)$ is exactly the weightwise dual lower-basis functional with that label. [F1, F2]

2.1 Identification with the upper global basis. The integral projective identification [F3] identifies the tensor form on projectives with the actual highest-weight contravariant form; the upper/lower duality theorem identifies these restricted dual functionals with the upper global vectors and preserves crystal labels. This proves the bijection and the normalization statements, using neither a generic negative-half form nor a vector-dual trace shift. [step 1.1, F3]

3.1 Cover/simple correspondence and the two actions. A simple and its normalized projective cover have the same $B(\Lambda)$ label by the cover/simple correspondence of [F2], not by applying projective Hom duality to a simple. The $G_0$ theorem [F3] proves the canonical action and its defect-rescaled KK version; keeping the two maps distinct preserves both sound quantum actions and the rank-one $\lambda=2$ check, with $\Psi_{\mathrm{KK}}=q^{\operatorname{def}_\Lambda(\beta)}\Psi_{\mathrm{can}}$ on root $\beta$, so that only $\Psi_{\mathrm{can}}$ gives the unrescaled upper-basis claim. The Axiom of Choice is inherited through the QG-5 global-basis duality and the generic basis suppliers of [F2] and [F3]. [step 2.1, F2, F3] ∎

items.title: Cyclotomic KLR quotients in ranks zero, one and two
items.statement:
Work over any field $k$ with a real symmetrizable Cartan datum, arbitrary symmetrizers $d_i$, dominant $\Lambda$ and the STANDARD homogeneous polynomials $a_i=u^{\lambda_i}$.
(a) $R^\Lambda(0)=k$ has one normalized simple and projective, the vacuum.
(b) For every color $i$, $R^\Lambda(\alpha_i)=k[x]/x^{\lambda_i}$ with $\deg x=2d_i$ and graded dimension $\sum_{r=0}^{\lambda_i-1}q^{2d_ir}$ when $\lambda_i\ge1$. Its unique normalized simple is $k$, its normalized projective HOM-self-dual cover is the regular module, and the coefficient-of-$x^{\lambda_i-1}$ Frobenius FUNCTIONAL has degree $-2d_i(\lambda_i-1)$. If $\lambda_i=0$ the block is zero and has NO simple; if $\lambda_i=1$ it is $k$.
(c) In rank one $I=\{i\}$, at EVERY $n\ge0$ the algebra is the cyclotomic nil-Hecke quotient $NH_n/(x_1^{\lambda_i})$. It is nonzero precisely for $0\le n\le\lambda_i$. At each such root it has exactly one normalized self-dual simple, and zero blocks have none; hence there are $\lambda_i+1$ normalized simple classes in total, matching the rank-one highest-weight module. For $1\le n\le\lambda_i$ its symmetric corner is $k[e_1,\ldots,e_n]/(h_{\lambda_i-n+1},\ldots,h_{\lambda_i})$, the graded Grassmannian coinvariant ring, and the algebra is the associated graded polynomial-column matrix algebra. The normalized simple column has graded dimension $[n]_{q_i}!$, where $q_i=q^{d_i}$.
(d) Explicitly at $\lambda_i=2,n=2$, the block is $\operatorname{End}_k(C\{-d_i\})$ with $C=k[x_1,x_2]/(x_1+x_2,x_1x_2)$, its basis $1,x_1$ in degrees $0,2d_i$. Its unique self-dual simple $S_2=C\{-d_i\}$ has graded dimension $q_i^{-1}+q_i$ and is also the normalized indecomposable projective $P_2$. It is NOT a one-dimensional module with both dots zero. The regular class is $[R^\Lambda(2\alpha_i)]=[2]_{q_i}[P_2]$ in $K_0$ and $[2]_{q_i}[S_2]$ in $G_0$.
(e) Arbitrary monic $a_i$ gives the ungraded deformation: $\lambda_i=2$, $a_i=u(u-1)$ gives $k\oplus k$ at root $\alpha_i$. Ordinary finiteness/symmetry remain true, but this is not the standard graded $V(2)$ identification.

items.title: Self-dual shift normalization for a cyclotomic projective
items.statement:
For rank one $d_i=1$ and $\lambda\ge1$, let $B=k[x]/x^\lambda$ and $P=B$. The PROJECTIVE Hom dual satisfies $P^\#\cong P$, so the canonical normalized projective is $P$ with no shift. Its finite vector dual is different:
$$D_\psi P\cong P\{-2(\lambda-1)\}.$$
The unique vector-dual-centered shift of this regular module is $P\{-(\lambda-1)\}$. For $\lambda=1$ both centers agree; for $\lambda=2$, projective Hom-self-duality centers $P$ at $0$ while vector-self-duality centers it at $-1$. If $\lambda=0$ the block is zero and there is no indecomposable projective here. For any normalized cyclotomic projective the general relation is $D_\psi P\cong P^\#\{-2\operatorname{def}_\Lambda(\beta)\}$; it does not redefine the lower-basis projective normalization.
items.strategy: Evaluation $\operatorname{HOM}_B(B,B)\cong B$ gives the projective dual directly, with the generator-fixing anti-involution producing the same left module. The coefficient-of-$x^{\lambda-1}$ trace has degree $-2(\lambda-1)$ and its perfect anti-diagonal pairing identifies $D_\psi B$ with $B$ in that NEGATIVE shift. Since $D_\psi(P\{s\})=D_\psi P\{-s\}$, vector self-duality solves $-2(\lambda-1)-s=s$, namely $s=-(\lambda-1)$. Projective Hom self-duality instead solves $-s=s$, namely $s=0$. These distinct finite calculations establish uniqueness of each center and their stated examples. The symmetric-algebra theorem gives the general defect shift after the independent projective normalization; no trace halving is used to pick the lower-basis class.

items.title: The categorical $\mathfrak{sl}_2$ commutator in a small cyclotomic weight
items.statement:
Take $I=\{i\}$ with $(\alpha_i\mid\alpha_i)=2$, $d_i=1$, $q_i=q$, and
$\Lambda=2\Lambda_1$, so that $\langle h_i,\Lambda\rangle=2$ and the standard
cyclotomic quotient has relations $x_1^2e(\nu)=0$. Then:

(a) $R^\Lambda(0)=k$, $R^\Lambda(\alpha_i)=k[x_1]/(x_1^2)$ with graded
dimension $1+q^2$, and $R^\Lambda(n\alpha_i)=0$ for $n\ge3$, so the functors
on the nonzero weights are $F^\Lambda_ik=R^\Lambda(\alpha_i)$ and
$F^\Lambda_iE^\Lambda_ik=0$;

(b) the categorical $\mathfrak{sl}_2$ relation of
[[thm-cyclotomic-klr-sl-two-categorical-commutator]] at $\beta=0$,
$\lambda=\Lambda$ (case $\langle h_i,\lambda\rangle=2\ge0$) reads
$q^{-2}F^\Lambda_iE^\Lambda_i\oplus\mathrm{Id}\oplus q^2\mathrm{Id}\cong
E^\Lambda_iF^\Lambda_i$; on the vacuum it says
$E^\Lambda_iF^\Lambda_ik\cong k\oplus k\{2\}$, which is exactly
$R^\Lambda(\alpha_i)\cong k\oplus k\{2\}$;

(c) consequently, with the normalized operators of
[[thm-cyclotomic-klr-functors-define-an-integrable-quantum-action-on-k-zero-and-g-zero]],
on $[\mathrm{Proj}(R^\Lambda(0))]$: $E_iF_i[1_\Lambda]=(q+q^{-1})[1_\Lambda]$
and $F_iE_i[1_\Lambda]=0$, so
$[E_i,F_i][1_\Lambda]=(q+q^{-1})[1_\Lambda]
=(K_i-K_i^{-1})/(q_i-q_i^{-1})[1_\Lambda]$ with
$K_i[1_\Lambda]=q^2[1_\Lambda]$; on $[\mathrm{Rep}(R^\Lambda(0))]$ the same
commutator identity holds: $F_i[k]=q^{-1}[k\oplus k\{2\}]$, $E_i$ lowers back,
$F_iE_i[k]=0$, and $E_iF_i[k]=(q+q^{-1})[k]$. This is the mixed relation of
[[thm-cyclotomic-klr-functors-define-an-integrable-quantum-action-on-k-zero-and-g-zero]]
verified at the first nontrivial weight.

items.title: Word projectives need not give lower global basis vectors
items.statement:
Once the isomorphism $[\mathrm{Proj}(R^\Lambda)]\cong V_A(\Lambda)$ of
[[thm-cyclotomic-klr-projective-k-zero-is-the-integral-highest-weight-module]]
is known, the classes of the word projectives $R^\Lambda(\beta)e(\nu)$ are
automatically lower global basis vectors.
items.strategy:
At root $2\alpha_i$ the regular word projective has the graded decomposition
$$R^\Lambda(2\alpha_i)\cong P_{i,2}\{1\}\oplus P_{i,2}\{-1\},\qquad [R^\Lambda(2\alpha_i)]=(q+q^{-1})[P_{i,2}].$$

Under the vacuum-normalized identification the word class is $F_i^2v_{2\Lambda_1}$, whereas the lower global vector is $F_i^{(2)}v_{2\Lambda_1}$. Their ratio $q+q^{-1}$ is a nonunit of $A=\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$. The normalized indecomposable divided-power projective gives the lower vector in this weight; the ordinary word projective does not.

1.1 The word class. By [F1] the word projective decomposes as $(q+q^{-1})$ copies of $P_{i,2}$, so $[R^\Lambda(2\alpha_i)]=(q+q^{-1})[P_{i,2}]$; under the K_0 isomorphism of the integral projective theorem this is the class of the ordinary product $F_i^2v_{2\Lambda_1}$. [F1]

1.2 In the rank-one module $V(2\Lambda_1)$, the Kashiwara string is $v,F_iv,F_i^{(2)}v$. These vectors generate its zero chart; they are bar fixed and generate the corresponding infinity chart. In weight $2\alpha_i$ the divided-power integral lattice is $AF_i^{(2)}v$: any divided word of that weight is an $A$-multiple of $F_i^{(2)}v$, since $F_i^2v=[2]_iF_i^{(2)}v$. Since an integral Laurent polynomial regular at both $0$ and infinity is an integer constant, the balanced intersection in that weight is $\mathbb ZF_i^{(2)}v$, and its positive string residue selects $F_i^{(2)}v$ as the lower global lift. [F2, algebra]

2.1 By [F2], $F_i^2v=[2]_iF_i^{(2)}v$. The coefficient $[2]_i=q+q^{-1}$ is a nonunit: evaluation at $q=1$ sends it to $2$, while an invertible Laurent polynomial must evaluate to a unit of $\mathbb Z$. Hence the word class cannot be the lower global vector identified in step 1.2. [step 1.1, step 1.2, F2, algebra]

3.1 This refutes the assertion that word-projective classes are automatically lower global vectors. Here the integral divided-power class $[P_{i,2}]$ gives $F_i^{(2)}v$ directly, whereas the regular word class has the nonunit coefficient $q+q^{-1}$. The finite example makes no general impossibility claim about extracting a basis from additional categorical or quantum-module structure. [step 1.1, step 1.2, step 2.1] ∎

items.title: The projective-simple Cartan pairing in a small cyclotomic block
items.statement:
For rank one $d_i=1$, $\lambda=2$, let $B_r=R^\Lambda(r\alpha_i)$. The
normalized simples are $S_0=k$, $S_1=k$ with $x=0$, and
$S_2=C\{-1\}$ of graded dimension $q^{-1}+q$, where
$C=k[x_1,x_2]/(x_1+x_2,x_1x_2)$. Their normalized projective covers are
$P_0=k$, $P_1=k[x]/x^2$, $P_2=S_2$. Then $T(P_r,S_s)=\delta_{rs}$, with
distinct roots paired by zero. Under the integral projective identification
$P_0,P_1,P_2$ map to $v,Fv,F^{(2)}v$, respectively, while
$[B_2]=(q+q^{-1})[P_2]$ maps to $F^2v$. In $G_0$ the correct regular classes
are $[B_1]=(1+q^2)[S_1]$ and $[B_2]=(q+q^{-1})[S_2]$. The canonical
restricted-dual map sends $S_r$ to the form-dual of the corresponding divided
lower vector; it does not identify $B_1$ with $S_1$.
